docs.text: GlitchyGames is a wrapper around Pygame that aims to support 20-25FPS minimum games on Raspberry Pi and other low powered Linux systems. The engine is written to provide: Readability as a first principle Scene primitives Advanced event handling Human readable/editable sprite file formats Example Game # Let's make a new game called Bitrot Adventures. The goal of our game will be to draw a pixel on the screen and handle key events to move the pixel around. #!/usr/bin/env python3 """Bitrot Adventures""" import argparse import pygame from glitchygames.engine import GameEngine from glitchygames.scenes import Scene class BitrotAdventures ( Scene ): """Draws a pixel to the screen""" def __init__ ( self , options ): super () . __init__ ( options = options , groups = None ) def main (): GameEngine () . start () if __name__ == "__main__" : main ()

docs.text: Galimore (1998–2001): what it is and how its tools work # A survey of the Galimore project (1998–2001), the author's earlier game and its tools, made on 2026-10-18 to inform GlitchyGames' level tools ( plans/2026-10-18-level-tools.md ). Conventions: SRC/ = the original files ( galimore_files/ , kept outside this repository); X/ = where the survey extracted each archive (one directory per archive). [read] = read directly in a file; [inferred] = concluded from sizes, layouts or context. R/ = PNG renders the survey decoded from the original data with a small read-only decoder, used to confirm the binary layouts below (the decoder and renders are not in this repository). Nothing from the archives was executed. TL;DR # Not a Mac game. Galimore is a top-down tile RPG ("similar to Final Fantasy 3 (English) or Zelda", Galimore Clean Up/Old Galimore Folder/Galimore Archive/public_html copy/index.html ) [read] for MS-DOS , developed on an iMac (Photoshop 5.02 for art, Virtual PC for code: "Yeah, I'm using a Mac to write a PC game", public_html copy/development.html ) [read]. Hence the resource forks, MacBinary .bin , CR line endings and ƒ folder names. Two engine generations: 1999, Borland C++ 16-bit DOS : BGI SVGA256.BGI , 256 colours, XMS. A playable GALIMORE.EXE plus tools GEDIT, GMAP, GATTRIB, MAKEDAT, GTORAW/RAWTOG ( X/CU_galisource072399/ ) [read]. Aug 1999 – Aug 2000, DJGPP (gcc 2.8.1) + Allegro 3.9.32 WIP , 640×480 at 16/15-bit colour. Only the toolchain exists: Galibmap (bitmap/sprite editor), Mapedit (map editor), Galimake (data packer) and a fire-effect demo. The new game was "Not yet started, but should use most of the mapeditor engine" ( development.html ) [read]. Successor: in Aug 2000 the code was relicensed (LGPL) as "RPG Tools" / "Phosphor" , a SourceForge map editor ( Galimore/Old Galimore Folder/RPG Tools Code/ ) [read]; only headers and a Makefile exist (no rendering code; graphics were Allegro 2D, with no OpenGL anywhere). Formats: every file is a raw fwrite dump of a C++ object: no header, no version, little-endian, compiler-specific padding. File type is detected purely by size (2332 / 49152 / 3072 / 4608 bytes). All are fully decoded in §2. 1. Code: 297 .h , 293 .cpp , 75 .o , 25 .gpr + 25 .gdt (RHIDE), 14 .exe . Other: 34 .zip , 11 .map , 10 .dat , 19 .html , 8 .log , ~21 extension-less Mac sound files. .raw sizes: 675 × 3072 (32×32 RGB), 44 × 4608 (32×48 RGB), 118 × 768 (16×16 RGB), 4 × 6144, 4 × 4170. 1.4 Not extracted / unreadable / skipped # Zip members inside ƒ folders failed ("Illegal byte sequence"); their unpacked copies were read. 060400.zip member test<non-ASCII> (a 49,152 B sprite). Nested gbe_4_17_00.zip , gme_4_17_00.zip , gali.zip (May 2000 archive). No unar / lsar ; no StuffIt/BinHex archives found in scope. Sounds: data forks are 0 bytes; audio is only in resource forks ( sfil , System 7 sound). ClarisWorks design docs read via strings only (fragmentary). .psd / .psp / .big identified, not viewed. Skipped as personal: a personal page in public_html copy/ and an e-mail contacts file in RPG Tools Code/ . 2. Tools and file formats # All written with ofstream::write((char*)&obj, sizeof(obj)) , little-endian x86. 2.1 Galibmap: bitmap and sprite editor (2000) # Sources src/galibmap.cpp , src/bmap_gui.cpp , src/gmore_raw.cpp , src/g_object.cpp , src/g_sprite.cpp ; binary X/bitmap_Binary/galibmap.exe . - Space toggles object mode (8 frames of 32×32) and sprite mode (16 frames of 32×48). - 6× zoomed canvas: left-drag paints, right-drag eyedropper; drag frames in the strip to copy or reorder. - R/G/B sliders, three colour wells (C cycles, R replaces colour 2 with colour 1); New / Save / Load / Quit; keys 1–8, N, L, S, Esc. - Load branches purely on file_size : 2332 → object, 49152 → sprite, 3072 → raw tile, 4608 → raw sprite frame (the file browser filters by the same sizes). GALIMORE_OBJECT (tile/object), 2332 bytes ( .bg , .fg , .get ): | Offset | Size | Field | |---|---|---| | 0 | 2048 | INT16 array[32][32] , [x][y] (offset (x·32+y)·2), RGB565 ; 0xF81F = transparent | | 2048 | 21 | objectName | | 2069 | 1 | objectType | | 2070 | 1 | objectState | | 2071 | 1 | objectSpecial | | 2072 | 2 | objectIsUsableBy (UINT16) | | 2074 | 1 | objectWeight | | 2075 | 256 | objectDescription | | 2331 | 1 | pad | The attribute block is all zeros in every shipped .dat (never authored). GALIMORE_SPRITE, 49,152 bytes ( .spr ): 16 × short array[32][48] , [x][y] RGB565. Frame plan ( spriteguide.html ): front / away / side × still / walk-R / walk-L, side mirrored → 9 used. pockets.spr uses 6 (rest grey). RAW, 3072 / 4608 bytes ( .raw ): headerless 8-bit RGB, row-major , 32×32 or 32×48 (Photoshop Raw export). Pipeline: Photoshop → .raw → Galibmap → .bg/.fg/.get/.spr . 2.2 Galimake: data packer # .dat = 2332-byte records back to back (58,300 = 25×2332, 67,628 = 29×2332, 4,664 = 2×2332). Stable tile IDs: maps store 1-based indices; on update Galimake loads the existing .dat , zeros (doesn't delete) records whose pixels no longer match a file , refreshes matches, and puts new tiles in the first blank slot, so map indices never shift. 2.3 Mapedit: map editor # Sources src/mapedit.cpp , src/mapeditor_gui.cpp , src/g_map.cpp , include/g_map.h . - 14×14 map view with scroll bars; 4×6 tile palette; layer tabs Fgnd / Bgnd / Obj / Spr / Mask ; floor radios 1F / 2F with show-layer checkboxes; "Make a Mask" and "Eraser" (tile 0). - Brush sizes 1–4; s / l save / load; Esc quits. - Mask tab: drag to stamp, right-click to pick up; magenta = no mask, purple = current, black = other. - Mask bits: 0 LAYER_SWITCH, 1 UNPASSABLE_GOOD, 2 UNPASSABLE_BAD, 3 UNPASSABLE_NEUTRAL, 4 DEEP, 5 BRIDGE, 6 CHASM, 7 PUSHABLE, 8 TRANSPARENT. An older plan ( g_mask.h , Dec 1999) added exits, burnable/bombable/freezable, hot/cold, anti-magic, death, door, soil, farmed, layer 2; "Mask Cases" planned a replacement tile in the upper 16 bits (e.g. burnt version) — never implemented. GALIMORE_MAP, 114,692 bytes (arrays [floor][x][y] ; verified by decoding house.map ): | Offset | Size | Field | |---|---|---| | 0 | 1 | landscape (always 0) | | 1 | 8192 | UINT8 fgLayer[2][64][64] (N → record N-1 of fg.dat ; 0 = empty) | | 8193 | 8192 | UINT8 bgLayer → bg.dat | | 16385 | 1 | pad | | 16386 | 16384 | UINT16 objectLayer → get.dat | | 32770 | 16384 | UINT16 spriteLayer (unimplemented) | | 49154 | 2 | pad | | 49156 | 65536 | UINT64 maskLayer | 64×64 cells per floor, 2 floors. Samples: house.map (cottage on grass, 14 fg tiles, 1 object, 40 fully-impassable mask cells), map.map (lattice test), test.map (18 cells of tile 1). 2.4 The 1999 tools # GEDIT (32×32, 256 colours, rotate/mirror/replace/transparent colour, 8-frame sprites); GMAP (15×15 maps, layer toggles, exits); GATTRIB (attributes); GTORAW / RAWTOG (bitmap ↔ RGB raw, palette as a switch ). The two DOCs are swapped ( GMAP.DOC documents GEDIT). - Bitmap, 1312 B: bitmapSize, transparentImage, transparencyColor (default 15); byte array[32][32] palette indices [x][y] ; attribs (name[21], 3 type bytes, misc, weight, description[256]). BKG.DAT 19,680 = 15×1312. - Sprite, 9262 B: 8 frames (DOWN½, UP½, LEFT½, RIGHT½) + speed, dimensions, direction, X, Y + temp array + struct time . - Map: 1458 B = unsigned char Map[6][15][15] + 6 exits (old: 2808 B with int ). Exit = name[13] + pad + int X, Y. Layers: background, wall, object, scenery, door. 3. Assets # Asset Where Format 2000 tile art 7_31_00/raw/ , Galimore Archive/Galimore Tiles/ , Galimore Specs/Galimore Tiles/ 32×32 / 16×16 RGB raw 2000 game tiles 7_31_00/bg (25), fg (29), get (2); X/mapedit_Binary/*.dat 2332 B objects ( R/bg.png , R/fg.png , R/get.png ) Maps X/mapedit_Binary/{house,map,test}.map 114,692 B ( R/house_crop.png , R/map_crop.png ) Sprites pockets.spr , Sprite Testing/pockets_*.raw , Galimore Sprites/* .spr , raw, .psd , .gif ( R/pockets.png ) Objects / icons Galimore Objects/* , The 5 Points/* .psd / .psp World design Continent*.psd , Experiment Town.psd , House Example.jpg Photoshop 1999 art X/CU_galisource072399/ (70 bitmaps; sprites JABBA/MONK/MONST/PIMP/DOUG/MAN) 1312 B bitmaps, 9262 B sprites Sound Sound Effects/Stephen King/ (21) Mac resource forks only 4. Code quality and notable points # Good ideas: stable tile IDs (blank instead of delete); size-based type sniffing; Allegro driver trimming; reusable ID-dispatched widget toolkit with a "GUI Shell" starter template; per-function debug gating; Photoshop RAW interop; two-floor maps with a 64-bit per-cell property mask and layer-switch bit; palette-gradient fire for animated tiles; the editor doubles as the renderer. Bugs spotted (reported, not changed): 1. g_map.cpp saveMap() / loadMap() : char *fileName; strcpy(fileName, …) (uninitialized pointer). 2. g_map.cpp drawATile() : uninitialized theTileVector , no default: case. 3. mapeditor_gui.cpp : visibleLayers bit layouts disagree, and init uses && for & . 4. "Transparent" mask checkbox has no handler. 5. GALIMORE_OBJECT::getBitmap() has no return . 6. convertTo15() is identical to convertTo16() . 7. Sprite-frame copy constructor copies only 32×32 of 32×48; displayFrame() size mismatch. 8. Attribute copy/assignment skip objectWeight . 9. ~GALIMORE_BITMAP_OBJECT destroys bitmaps shared by vector copies. 10. g_mask.h constants are unsigned short but shift up to bit 25 (bits ≥ 16 are zero). 11. loadDataFile dedups by pixels, so identical tiles would collapse [inferred risk]. 12. do{}while(infile) processes the failed final read once more. 13. .dat order depends on directory order; memory-dump formats are compiler/endian-specific. Unfinished: no 2000-era game runtime; sprite layer; object attributes; mask replacement tiles; Linux port; script editor, character generation, NPC AI, OpenPlay networking. RPG Tools / Phosphor (Aug 2000): rpg_map.h (map class renamed C_RPGMap ), rpg_raw.h (LGPL), gcc Makefile, a CodeWarrior project (the only real classic-Mac toolchain artefact), CVS at cvs.rpgtools.sourceforge.net , naming style in Text Docs/CODING_STYLE.txt ( C_ classes, S_ structs, g globals, k / gk constants). 5. Relevance to GlitchyGames # Roadmap #11 "Level/room data format (and tilemaps)" is open; each game rolls its own ScreenData / FloorData / LevelManager ( plans/engine-audit.md ). 5.1 Worth porting # Map model for #11: Galimore's ordered layers (bg → fg → objects → actors), per-cell properties kept separate from the art, and named exits with entry points. The GlitchyGames design built from these ideas, adjusted for today's games and constraints (object layers, a typed property vocabulary, exit regions with named spawn points), is plans/2026-10-18-level-tools-a-tilemap-format.md . Stable tile IDs: explicit IDs or tombstones, never list position. Collision on the map cell, separate from the art. Editor features: Mapedit's brush sizes, property-paint mode with pick-up/stamp, layer and floor visibility, tileset palette, eraser = 0; Galibmap's colour wells, frame drag-reorder, and the 9-frame walk-cycle convention. Animated tiles via animation frames, or a procedural fire buffer. 5.2 Converting Galimore data # The survey's read-only decoder (not in this repository) decodes everything below to PNG; sub-plan E ( plans/2026-10-18-level-tools-e-galimore-import.md ) plans a reviewed converter. - Tiles: <1024H , transpose from [x][y] , RGB565 → RGB888, 0xF81F → magenta; write TOML pixels + [colors] (10–60 colours per tile); keep the 1-based .dat index as the tile ID. - Sprites: 16 × 32×48 frames ( <1536H , [x][y] ); drop all-grey frames; walk_down (0–2), walk_up (3–5), walk_side (6–8, mirrored). - Raw: RGB888 row-major → PNG for Bitmappy. - Maps: offsets in §2.3; layers per floor; mask bits → named properties. - 1999 data: 1312 B indexed bitmaps (palette from GTORAW or GALIMORE PALLETE.GIF ; honour transparencyColor ), 9262 B 8-frame sprites, 1458 / 2808 B maps with exits — the best test case for a room/exit design. - Caveats: tiles may be RGB555 if saved in 15-bit mode; attribute blocks are empty; sounds need resource-fork extraction first (e.g. DeRez ).

docs.text: Sources src/galibmap.cpp , src/bmap_gui.cpp , src/gmore_raw.cpp , src/g_object.cpp , src/g_sprite.cpp ; binary X/bitmap_Binary/galibmap.exe . - Space toggles object mode (8 frames of 32×32) and sprite mode (16 frames of 32×48). - 6× zoomed canvas: left-drag paints, right-drag eyedropper; drag frames in the strip to copy or reorder. - R/G/B sliders, three colour wells (C cycles, R replaces colour 2 with colour 1); New / Save / Load / Quit; keys 1–8, N, L, S, Esc. - Load branches purely on file_size : 2332 → object, 49152 → sprite, 3072 → raw tile, 4608 → raw sprite frame (the file browser filters by the same sizes). GALIMORE_OBJECT (tile/object), 2332 bytes ( .bg , .fg , .get ): | Offset | Size | Field | |---|---|---| | 0 | 2048 | INT16 array[32][32] , [x][y] (offset (x·32+y)·2), RGB565 ; 0xF81F = transparent | | 2048 | 21 | objectName | | 2069 | 1 | objectType | | 2070 | 1 | objectState | | 2071 | 1 | objectSpecial | | 2072 | 2 | objectIsUsableBy (UINT16) | | 2074 | 1 | objectWeight | | 2075 | 256 | objectDescription | | 2331 | 1 | pad | The attribute block is all zeros in every shipped .dat (never authored). GALIMORE_SPRITE, 49,152 bytes ( .spr ): 16 × short array[32][48] , [x][y] RGB565. Frame plan ( spriteguide.html ): front / away / side × still / walk-R / walk-L, side mirrored → 9 used. pockets.spr uses 6 (rest grey). RAW, 3072 / 4608 bytes ( .raw ): headerless 8-bit RGB, row-major , 32×32 or 32×48 (Photoshop Raw export). Pipeline: Photoshop → .raw → Galibmap → .bg/.fg/.get/.spr .

docs.text: .dat = 2332-byte records back to back (58,300 = 25×2332, 67,628 = 29×2332, 4,664 = 2×2332). Stable tile IDs: maps store 1-based indices; on update Galimake loads the existing .dat , zeros (doesn't delete) records whose pixels no longer match a file , refreshes matches, and puts new tiles in the first blank slot, so map indices never shift.

docs.text: Sources src/mapedit.cpp , src/mapeditor_gui.cpp , src/g_map.cpp , include/g_map.h . - 14×14 map view with scroll bars; 4×6 tile palette; layer tabs Fgnd / Bgnd / Obj / Spr / Mask ; floor radios 1F / 2F with show-layer checkboxes; "Make a Mask" and "Eraser" (tile 0). - Brush sizes 1–4; s / l save / load; Esc quits. - Mask tab: drag to stamp, right-click to pick up; magenta = no mask, purple = current, black = other. - Mask bits: 0 LAYER_SWITCH, 1 UNPASSABLE_GOOD, 2 UNPASSABLE_BAD, 3 UNPASSABLE_NEUTRAL, 4 DEEP, 5 BRIDGE, 6 CHASM, 7 PUSHABLE, 8 TRANSPARENT. An older plan ( g_mask.h , Dec 1999) added exits, burnable/bombable/freezable, hot/cold, anti-magic, death, door, soil, farmed, layer 2; "Mask Cases" planned a replacement tile in the upper 16 bits (e.g. burnt version) — never implemented. GALIMORE_MAP, 114,692 bytes (arrays [floor][x][y] ; verified by decoding house.map ): | Offset | Size | Field | |---|---|---| | 0 | 1 | landscape (always 0) | | 1 | 8192 | UINT8 fgLayer[2][64][64] (N → record N-1 of fg.dat ; 0 = empty) | | 8193 | 8192 | UINT8 bgLayer → bg.dat | | 16385 | 1 | pad | | 16386 | 16384 | UINT16 objectLayer → get.dat | | 32770 | 16384 | UINT16 spriteLayer (unimplemented) | | 49154 | 2 | pad | | 49156 | 65536 | UINT64 maskLayer | 64×64 cells per floor, 2 floors. Samples: house.map (cottage on grass, 14 fg tiles, 1 object, 40 fully-impassable mask cells), map.map (lattice test), test.map (18 cells of tile 1).

docs.text: GEDIT (32×32, 256 colours, rotate/mirror/replace/transparent colour, 8-frame sprites); GMAP (15×15 maps, layer toggles, exits); GATTRIB (attributes); GTORAW / RAWTOG (bitmap ↔ RGB raw, palette as a switch ). The two DOCs are swapped ( GMAP.DOC documents GEDIT). - Bitmap, 1312 B: bitmapSize, transparentImage, transparencyColor (default 15); byte array[32][32] palette indices [x][y] ; attribs (name[21], 3 type bytes, misc, weight, description[256]). BKG.DAT 19,680 = 15×1312. - Sprite, 9262 B: 8 frames (DOWN½, UP½, LEFT½, RIGHT½) + speed, dimensions, direction, X, Y + temp array + struct time . - Map: 1458 B = unsigned char Map[6][15][15] + 6 exits (old: 2808 B with int ). Exit = name[13] + pad + int X, Y. Layers: background, wall, object, scenery, door.

docs.title: 3. Assets

docs.text: Good ideas: stable tile IDs (blank instead of delete); size-based type sniffing; Allegro driver trimming; reusable ID-dispatched widget toolkit with a "GUI Shell" starter template; per-function debug gating; Photoshop RAW interop; two-floor maps with a 64-bit per-cell property mask and layer-switch bit; palette-gradient fire for animated tiles; the editor doubles as the renderer. Bugs spotted (reported, not changed): 1. g_map.cpp saveMap() / loadMap() : char *fileName; strcpy(fileName, …) (uninitialized pointer). 2. g_map.cpp drawATile() : uninitialized theTileVector , no default: case. 3. mapeditor_gui.cpp : visibleLayers bit layouts disagree, and init uses && for & . 4. "Transparent" mask checkbox has no handler. 5. GALIMORE_OBJECT::getBitmap() has no return . 6. convertTo15() is identical to convertTo16() . 7. Sprite-frame copy constructor copies only 32×32 of 32×48; displayFrame() size mismatch. 8. Attribute copy/assignment skip objectWeight . 9. ~GALIMORE_BITMAP_OBJECT destroys bitmaps shared by vector copies. 10. g_mask.h constants are unsigned short but shift up to bit 25 (bits ≥ 16 are zero). 11. loadDataFile dedups by pixels, so identical tiles would collapse [inferred risk]. 12. do{}while(infile) processes the failed final read once more. 13. .dat order depends on directory order; memory-dump formats are compiler/endian-specific. Unfinished: no 2000-era game runtime; sprite layer; object attributes; mask replacement tiles; Linux port; script editor, character generation, NPC AI, OpenPlay networking. RPG Tools / Phosphor (Aug 2000): rpg_map.h (map class renamed C_RPGMap ), rpg_raw.h (LGPL), gcc Makefile, a CodeWarrior project (the only real classic-Mac toolchain artefact), CVS at cvs.rpgtools.sourceforge.net , naming style in Text Docs/CODING_STYLE.txt ( C_ classes, S_ structs, g globals, k / gk constants).

docs.title: 5. Relevance to GlitchyGames

docs.text: Map model for #11: Galimore's ordered layers (bg → fg → objects → actors), per-cell properties kept separate from the art, and named exits with entry points. The GlitchyGames design built from these ideas, adjusted for today's games and constraints (object layers, a typed property vocabulary, exit regions with named spawn points), is plans/2026-10-18-level-tools-a-tilemap-format.md . Stable tile IDs: explicit IDs or tombstones, never list position. Collision on the map cell, separate from the art. Editor features: Mapedit's brush sizes, property-paint mode with pick-up/stamp, layer and floor visibility, tileset palette, eraser = 0; Galibmap's colour wells, frame drag-reorder, and the 9-frame walk-cycle convention. Animated tiles via animation frames, or a procedural fire buffer.
docs.title: 5.1 Worth porting

docs.text: The survey's read-only decoder (not in this repository) decodes everything below to PNG; sub-plan E ( plans/2026-10-18-level-tools-e-galimore-import.md ) plans a reviewed converter. - Tiles: <1024H , transpose from [x][y] , RGB565 → RGB888, 0xF81F → magenta; write TOML pixels + [colors] (10–60 colours per tile); keep the 1-based .dat index as the tile ID. - Sprites: 16 × 32×48 frames ( <1536H , [x][y] ); drop all-grey frames; walk_down (0–2), walk_up (3–5), walk_side (6–8, mirrored). - Raw: RGB888 row-major → PNG for Bitmappy. - Maps: offsets in §2.3; layers per floor; mask bits → named properties. - 1999 data: 1312 B indexed bitmaps (palette from GTORAW or GALIMORE PALLETE.GIF ; honour transparencyColor ), 9262 B 8-frame sprites, 1458 / 2808 B maps with exits — the best test case for a room/exit design. - Caveats: tiles may be RGB555 if saved in 15-bit mode; attribute blocks are empty; sounds need resource-fork extraction first (e.g. DeRez ).

docs.text: Multi-Controller System Documentation # Overview # The Multi-Controller System enables up to 4 simultaneous controllers to navigate and interact with the bitmappy tool independently. Each controller has its own visual indicator, navigation state, and can operate simultaneously without conflicts. Features # Multi-Controller Support : Up to 4 simultaneous controllers Independent Navigation : Each controller navigates film strips and frames independently Visual Distinction : Unique colored triangles for each controller (Red, Green, Blue, Yellow) Smart Positioning : Automatic collision avoidance when multiple controllers select the same frame State Preservation : Controllers maintain their selection state when switching between them Hotplug Support : Controllers can be connected/disconnected during operation Architecture # Core Components # MultiControllerManager - Central singleton managing all controllers ControllerSelection - Individual controller state management VisualCollisionManager - Smart positioning and collision avoidance Integration with Bitmappy - Event handling and film strip navigation Controller Color Scheme # Controller 0 : Red (255, 0, 0) Controller 1 : Green (0, 255, 0) Controller 2 : Blue (0, 0, 255) Controller 3 : Yellow (255, 255, 0) Usage Examples # Basic Setup # from glitchygames.tools.multi_controller_manager import MultiControllerManager from glitchygames.tools.controller_selection import ControllerSelection from glitchygames.tools.visual_collision_manager import VisualCollisionManager # Initialize the system manager = MultiControllerManager () visual_manager = VisualCollisionManager () controller_selections = {} # Set up a controller instance_id = 0 controller_id = manager . assign_controller ( instance_id ) controller_selections [ controller_id ] = ControllerSelection ( controller_id , instance_id ) Controller Activation # # Activate a controller controller_selections [ controller_id ] . activate () manager . activate_controller ( instance_id ) # Set initial selection controller_selections [ controller_id ] . set_selection ( "animation_name" , 0 ) # Add visual indicator visual_manager . add_controller_indicator ( controller_id = controller_id , instance_id = instance_id , color = manager . CONTROLLER_COLORS [ controller_id ], position = ( 100 , 100 ) ) Navigation # # Navigate to different animation/frame controller_selections [ controller_id ] . set_selection ( "new_animation" , 5 ) # Get current selection animation , frame = controller_selections [ controller_id ] . get_selection () print ( f "Controller { controller_id } is at { animation } , frame { frame } " ) # Get navigation history history = controller_selections [ controller_id ] . get_navigation_history () for entry in history : print ( f "Previous: { entry [ 'animation' ] } , frame { entry [ 'frame' ] } " ) Multi-Controller Navigation # # Set up multiple controllers for i in range ( 4 ): instance_id = i controller_id = manager . assign_controller ( instance_id ) controller_selections [ controller_id ] = ControllerSelection ( controller_id , instance_id ) controller_selections [ controller_id ] . activate () # Each controller can navigate independently controller_selections [ controller_id ] . set_selection ( f "animation_ { i } " , i ) # Add visual indicators visual_manager . add_controller_indicator ( controller_id = controller_id , instance_id = instance_id , color = manager . CONTROLLER_COLORS [ controller_id ], position = ( 100 + i * 50 , 100 ) ) # All controllers can navigate independently controller_selections [ 0 ] . set_selection ( "animation_A" , 0 ) controller_selections [ 1 ] . set_selection ( "animation_B" , 1 ) controller_selections [ 2 ] . set_selection ( "animation_C" , 2 ) controller_selections [ 3 ] . set_selection ( "animation_D" , 3 ) Visual Collision Avoidance # # Multiple controllers at same position for i in range ( 3 ): visual_manager . add_controller_indicator ( controller_id = i , instance_id = i , color = ( 255 , 0 , 0 ), position = ( 100 , 100 ) # Same position ) # System automatically applies offsets to prevent overlap # Controller 0: (100, 100) - no offset # Controller 1: (85, 85) - (-15, -15) offset # Controller 2: (100, 100) - fallback offset Controller State Management # # Check controller status if manager . is_controller_active ( instance_id ): print ( f "Controller { instance_id } is active" ) # Get controller information info = manager . get_controller_info ( instance_id ) if info : print ( f "Controller { info . controller_id } : { info . status . value } " ) # Deactivate controller controller_selections [ controller_id ] . deactivate () manager . deactivate_controller ( instance_id ) Hotplug Support # # Handle controller connection def on_controller_connected ( instance_id ): controller_id = manager . assign_controller ( instance_id ) if controller_id is not None : controller_selections [ controller_id ] = ControllerSelection ( controller_id , instance_id ) print ( f "Controller { controller_id } connected" ) # Handle controller disconnection def on_controller_disconnected ( instance_id ): if instance_id in manager . assigned_controllers : controller_id = manager . assigned_controllers [ instance_id ] if controller_id in controller_selections : del controller_selections [ controller_id ] print ( f "Controller { controller_id } disconnected" ) Integration with Bitmappy # Event Handling # def handle_controller_event ( event ): """Handle controller events in bitmappy.""" if event . type == pygame . CONTROLLERBUTTONDOWN : controller_id = event . instance_id if event . button == pygame . CONTROLLER_BUTTON_A : # A button - select current frame if controller_id in controller_selections : controller_selections [ controller_id ] . activate () controller_selections [ controller_id ] . set_selection ( "current_animation" , 0 ) elif event . button == pygame . CONTROLLER_BUTTON_DPAD_LEFT : # D-pad left - previous frame if controller_id in controller_selections : current_animation , current_frame = controller_selections [ controller_id ] . get_selection () if current_frame > 0 : controller_selections [ controller_id ] . set_selection ( current_animation , current_frame - 1 ) elif event . button == pygame . CONTROLLER_BUTTON_DPAD_RIGHT : # D-pad right - next frame if controller_id in controller_selections : current_animation , current_frame = controller_selections [ controller_id ] . get_selection () controller_selections [ controller_id ] . set_selection ( current_animation , current_frame + 1 ) Film Strip Integration # def update_film_strip_indicators (): """Update visual indicators on film strips.""" for controller_id , selection in controller_selections . items (): if selection . is_active (): animation , frame = selection . get_selection () # Update visual indicator position if animation in film_strips : strip_position = film_strips [ animation ] . get_frame_position ( frame ) visual_manager . update_controller_position ( controller_id , strip_position ) Advanced Features # State Cloning # # Clone controller state to another controller source_controller = controller_selections [ 0 ] target_controller = controller_selections [ 1 ] source_controller . set_selection ( "animation_A" , 5 ) source_controller . clone_state_to ( target_controller ) # Target controller now has same state animation , frame = target_controller . get_selection () assert animation == "animation_A" assert frame == 5 Navigation History # # Track navigation history controller = controller_selections [ 0 ] controller . set_selection ( "animation1" , 0 ) controller . set_selection ( "animation2" , 1 ) controller . set_selection ( "animation3" , 2 ) # Get history history = controller . get_navigation_history () print ( f "Navigation history: { len ( history ) } entries" ) for entry in history : print ( f " { entry [ 'animation' ] } , frame { entry [ 'frame' ] } " ) Performance Optimization # # Clean up inactive controllers manager . cleanup_inactive_controllers () # Optimize visual positioning visual_manager . optimize_positioning () # Clear all indicators visual_manager . clear_all_indicators () Error Handling # Invalid Operations # # Handle invalid controller IDs gracefully if not manager . is_controller_active ( 999 ): print ( "Controller 999 not found" ) # Handle missing controller selections if controller_id not in controller_selections : print ( f "Controller { controller_id } not initialized" ) System Resilience # # System handles rapid controller switching for cycle in range ( 1000 ): for i in range ( 4 ): if i in controller_selections : controller_selections [ i ] . set_selection ( f "animation_ { i } " , cycle % 50 ) # System handles controller disconnection/reconnection for i in range ( 10 ): manager . _handle_controller_connect ( i ) # ... use controller ... manager . _handle_controller_disconnect ( i ) Best Practices # 1. Controller Lifecycle Management # def setup_controller ( instance_id ): """Properly set up a new controller.""" controller_id = manager . assign_controller ( instance_id ) if controller_id is not None : controller_selections [ controller_id ] = ControllerSelection ( controller_id , instance_id ) controller_selections [ controller_id ] . activate () manager . activate_controller ( instance_id ) return controller_id return None def cleanup_controller ( instance_id ): """Properly clean up a controller.""" if instance_id in manager . assigned_controllers : controller_id = manager . assigned_controllers [ instance_id ] if controller_id in controller_selections : controller_selections [ controller_id ] . deactivate () del controller_selections [ controller_id ] manager . deactivate_controller ( instance_id ) 2. Visual Indicator Management # def update_controller_visuals (): """Update all controller visual indicators.""" for controller_id , selection in controller_selections . items (): if selection . is_active (): animation , frame = selection . get_selection () position = get_frame_position ( animation , frame ) visual_manager . update_controller_position ( controller_id , position ) 3. State Synchronization # def sync_controller_states (): """Synchronize controller states with UI.""" for controller_id , selection in controller_selections . items (): if selection . is_active (): animation , frame = selection . get_selection () # Update UI elements update_film_strip_selection ( controller_id , animation , frame ) update_visual_indicator ( controller_id , animation , frame ) Troubleshooting # Common Issues # Controller not responding Check if controller is assigned: manager.assigned_controllers Verify controller is active: manager.is_controller_active(instance_id) Visual indicators overlapping System automatically handles collision avoidance Check collision groups: visual_manager.collision_groups State not preserved Ensure controller selection is activated: selection.activate() Check navigation history: selection.get_navigation_history() Debug Information # # Get system status print ( f "Active controllers: { manager . get_active_controllers () } " ) print ( f "Visual indicators: { len ( visual_manager . indicators ) } " ) print ( f "Collision groups: { len ( visual_manager . collision_groups ) } " ) # Get controller details for instance_id , info in manager . controllers . items (): print ( f "Controller { info . controller_id } : { info . status . value } , color { info . color } " ) Future Extensions # The multi-controller system provides a foundation for: Collaborative Editing : Multiple users editing simultaneously Advanced Visual Management : Custom indicators and positioning Session Management : Save/load controller configurations Permission Systems : Master/slave controller relationships API Reference # MultiControllerManager # assign_controller(instance_id) - Assign a controller ID activate_controller(instance_id) - Activate a controller is_controller_active(instance_id) - Check if controller is active get_controller_info(instance_id) - Get controller information get_active_controllers() - Get list of active controllers cleanup_inactive_controllers() - Clean up inactive controllers ControllerSelection # activate() - Activate the controller deactivate() - Deactivate the controller set_selection(animation, frame) - Set animation and frame get_selection() - Get current animation and frame get_navigation_history() - Get navigation history clone_state_to(other) - Clone state to another controller VisualCollisionManager # add_controller_indicator(controller_id, instance_id, color, position) - Add visual indicator remove_controller_indicator(controller_id) - Remove visual indicator update_controller_position(controller_id, position) - Update indicator position get_final_position(controller_id) - Get final position with offsets optimize_positioning() - Optimize all indicator positions

Command-Line Argument System # GlitchyGames uses a composable argparse architecture where the engine, event managers, font system, and individual games each contribute argument groups to a single parser. Every game built on the engine automatically inherits all engine-level flags, and can extend the parser with its own game-specific options. How Arguments Are Assembled # The orchestration happens in GameEngine.initialize_arguments() , called from GameEngine.__init__() . The flow is: sequenceDiagram participant GE as GameEngine.__init__() participant IA as initialize_arguments(game_class) participant AP as ArgumentParser participant ENGINE as GameEngine.args() participant MGR as Event Manager .args() x12 participant GAME as game_class.args() participant NS as Namespace GE->>IA: initialize_arguments(game_class) IA->>AP: ArgumentParser("GameName version X.Y") IA->>ENGINE: GameEngine.args(parser) Note over ENGINE: Adds "Graphics Options" group
14 arguments,
and "Diagnostics Options"
10 arguments ENGINE->>MGR: AppEventManager.args(parser) Note over MGR: Adds "App Options" group
(empty, reserved) ENGINE->>MGR: AudioEventManager.args(parser) Note over MGR: Adds "Sound Mixer Options" group
(empty, reserved) ENGINE->>MGR: ControllerEventManager.args(parser) Note over MGR: Adds "Controller Options" group
1 argument ENGINE->>MGR: DropEventManager.args(parser) Note over MGR: Adds "Drop Options" group
(empty, reserved) ENGINE->>MGR: FontManager.args(parser) Note over MGR: Adds "Font Options" group
7 arguments ENGINE->>MGR: GameEventManager.args(parser) Note over MGR: Adds "Game Options" group
3 arguments ENGINE->>MGR: JoystickEventManager.args(parser) Note over MGR: Adds "Joystick Options" group
(empty, reserved) ENGINE->>MGR: KeyboardEventManager.args(parser) Note over MGR: Adds "Keyboard Options" group
(empty, reserved) ENGINE->>MGR: MidiEventManager.args(parser) Note over MGR: Adds "Midi Options" group
(empty, reserved) ENGINE->>MGR: MouseEventManager.args(parser) Note over MGR: Adds "Mouse Options" group
(empty, reserved) ENGINE->>MGR: TouchEventManager.args(parser) Note over MGR: Adds "Touch Options" group
(empty, reserved) ENGINE->>MGR: WindowEventManager.args(parser) Note over MGR: Adds "Window Options" group
(empty, reserved) ENGINE-->>IA: return parser IA->>AP: parser.add_argument_group("GameName vX.Y Options") IA->>GAME: game_class.args(game_group) Note over GAME: Adds game-specific arguments
to its own group IA->>AP: parser.parse_args() AP-->>NS: Namespace with all arguments IA->>IA: GameEngine.OPTIONS = vars(args) IA->>IA: Derive synthetic: debug_events IA->>IA: Back-propagate: game.options = OPTIONS The Argument Group Hierarchy # Each layer adds its own add_argument_group() , producing clearly separated sections in --help output. The hierarchy mirrors the engine architecture. flowchart TD subgraph Parser["ArgumentParser: GameName version X.Y"] subgraph L1["Layer 1: Graphics Options (GameEngine)"] F1["-f, --target-fps"] F2["--fps-log-interval-ms"] F3["-w, --windowed"] F4["-r, --resolution"] F5["--use-gfxdraw"] F6["--update-type"] F7["--timer-backend"] F8["--sleep-granularity-ns"] F9["--windows-timer-1ms"] F16["--random-seed"] F17["--screen-shake-intensity, --rumble-intensity"] F18["--live-voice-pool"] F19["--video-driver"] end subgraph L1D["Layer 1: Diagnostics Options (GameEngine)"] D1["--log-timer-jitter, --perf-trim-percent, --fps-histogram"] D2["--debug-overlay"] D3["--record-trace, --replay-trace, --replay-fps"] D4["--audit, --replay-digest, --replay-pause-at-frame"] D5["--headless"] end subgraph L2["Layer 2: Event Manager Groups"] subgraph AO["App Options"] AO_EMPTY["(no arguments yet)"] end subgraph SM["Sound Mixer Options"] SM_EMPTY["(no arguments yet)"] end subgraph DO["Drop Options"] DO_EMPTY["(no arguments yet)"] end subgraph CO["Controller Options"] CO1["--input-mode"] end subgraph FO["Font Options"] FO1["--font-name"] FO2["--font-size"] FO3["--font-bold"] FO4["--font-italic"] FO5["--font-antialias"] FO6["--font-dpi"] FO7["--font-system"] end subgraph GO["Game Options"] GO1["-l, --log-level"] GO2["--no-unhandled-events"] GO3["-p, --profile"] end subgraph JO["Joystick Options"] JO_EMPTY["(no arguments yet)"] end subgraph KO["Keyboard Options"] KO_EMPTY["(no arguments yet)"] end subgraph MIO["Midi Options"] MIO_EMPTY["(no arguments yet)"] end subgraph MO["Mouse Options"] MO_EMPTY["(no arguments yet)"] end subgraph TO["Touch Options"] TO_EMPTY["(no arguments yet)"] end subgraph WO["Window Options"] WO_EMPTY["(no arguments yet)"] end end subgraph L3["Layer 3: Game-Specific Options"] GS["(varies per game)"] end end How Games Add Arguments # A game adds arguments by defining a @classmethod called args() on its scene class. The engine discovers this method via getattr(game, 'args', None) and calls it with a dedicated argument group. If the game does not define args() , the engine logs an informational message and continues. flowchart TD subgraph Engine["GameEngine.initialize_arguments()"] CHECK{"getattr(game, 'args', None)"} CHECK -->|"method exists"| GROUP["parser.add_argument_group( GameName vX.Y Options)"] GROUP --> CALL["game.args(group)"] CHECK -->|"None"| LOG["log.info: Game does not implement arguments"] end subgraph GameCode["Your Game Scene"] ARGS["@classmethod def args(cls, parser): parser.add_argument(...)"] end CALL --> ARGS Pattern: Minimal Game # class MyGame ( Scene ): NAME = 'My Game' VERSION = '1.0' @classmethod def args ( cls , parser ): parser . add_argument ( '-v' , '--version' , action = 'store_true' , help = 'print the game version and exit' , ) Pattern: Game with Custom Options # class JoystickDemo ( Scene ): NAME = 'Joystick Demo' VERSION = '1.0' @classmethod def args ( cls , parser ): parser . add_argument ( '--time' , type = int , default = 10 , help = 'time in seconds to wait before quitting' , ) parser . add_argument ( '-v' , '--version' , action = 'store_true' , help = 'print the game version and exit' , ) Note that the game receives an argument group , not the root parser. This means game arguments appear under their own heading in --help output. OPTIONS Dictionary Flow # After parsing, the Namespace is converted to a plain dict and propagated to every component that needs it. flowchart TD PARSE["parser.parse_args()"] --> VARS["vars(args) Namespace -> dict"] VARS --> OPT["GameEngine.OPTIONS (class var)"] OPT --> SYNTH{"log_level in DEBUG/CRITICAL/ERROR?"} SYNTH -->|"Yes"| DEBUG_T["OPTIONS['debug_events'] = True"] SYNTH -->|"No"| DEBUG_F["OPTIONS['debug_events'] = False"] DEBUG_T & DEBUG_F --> BACKPROP["game.options = OPTIONS"] BACKPROP --> SM_OPT["SceneManager.OPTIONS = OPTIONS"] SM_OPT --> SCENE_INIT["Scene.__init__(options=OPTIONS)"] SCENE_INIT --> SELF_OPT["self.options = OPTIONS"] subgraph Access["Runtime Access"] A1["self.options['target_fps']"] A2["self.options['font_name']"] A3["self.options['log_level']"] A4["self.options['debug_events']"] A5["GameEngine.OPTIONS['resolution']"] end SELF_OPT --> Access Complete Flag Reference # Graphics Options # Added by GameEngine.args() in glitchygames/engine/game_engine.py . Flag Type Default Description -f , --target-fps float None (the game's TARGET_FPS , else 60.01) Cap the framerate; 0 = uncapped --fps-log-interval-ms float 1000 How often to log the FPS counter in ms -w , --windowed store_true True Run in windowed mode (the default is already True , so the flag changes nothing) -r , --resolution str 800x480 Display resolution (WxH) --use-gfxdraw store_true False Use pygame.gfxdraw for rendering --update-type choice update Display update method: update or flip --timer-backend choice auto Timer backend: auto (the fast backend with this machine's sleep delay measured, so each sleep wakes in time), fast (assumes sleeps wake on time) or pygame (legacy) --sleep-granularity-ns int 1000000 How long before each frame deadline the fast backend is to wake from its sleep and spin (ns); 0 spins only --windows-timer-1ms store_true False On Windows, request 1ms system timer resolution --video-driver choice None Platform-specific video driver (see below) --random-seed int random 64-bit Master seed for every engine random stream --screen-shake-intensity float 1.0 Screen shake strength, 0.0 (off) to 1.0 --rumble-intensity float 1.0 Controller rumble strength, 0.0 (off) to 1.0 --live-voice-pool int 4 Mixer channels reserved for real-time synth voices --video-driver choices by platform: Platform Choices Linux wayland , x11 , dga , fbcon , directfb , ggi , vgl , svgalib , aalib Windows windib , directx macOS (none currently defined; the code checks platform.system() == 'MacOS' , which never matches, so macOS falls through to no choices either way) Diagnostics Options # Added by GameEngine.args() right after the Graphics Options: how any run is watched, recorded, replayed or diagnosed, whatever the game. They change no game settings. Flag Type Default Description --log-timer-jitter store_true False Log frame pacing jitter statistics periodically --perf-trim-percent float 5.0 Percent of frames to trim from top and bottom in FPS report --fps-histogram choice equal-range FPS histogram buckets in the shutdown report: equal-range or target-relative --debug-overlay / --no-debug-overlay bool False Show the debug overlay at startup (F3 toggles, F4 cycles panels) --record-trace PATH None Record the session to a gzip JSON Lines trace ( Gameplay Recording and Replay ) --replay-trace PATH None Replay a recording exactly, reporting the first divergence --replay-fps choice None (read as recorded ) With --replay-trace : FPS events from the recorded or the real frame times --audit / --no-audit bool False With --replay-trace : replay twice in fresh processes and compare (exit 0, 3 when nondeterministic, 70 when a run could not finish; see exit codes ) --replay-digest PATH None With --replay-trace : write a SHA-256 per replayed frame (used by --audit ) --replay-pause-at-frame N (non-negative int) None With --replay-trace , watched: skip the start screen, rebuild frames 0 to N - 1 unpresented, then pause with frame N next (what step back restarts with; ignored with --headless ; step back ) --headless store_true False Run on SDL's dummy video and audio drivers (no window, no sound); a replay also runs unpaced and prints its report to stdout ( headless runs ) Game Options # Added by GameEventManager.args() in glitchygames/events/game.py . Flag Type Default Description -l , --log-level choice info Logging level: debug , info , warning , error , critical --no-unhandled-events store_true False Raise UnhandledEventError on unhandled events -p , --profile store_true False Enable cProfile profiling Controller Options # Added by ControllerEventManager.args() in glitchygames/events/controller.py . Flag Type Default Description --input-mode choice auto Gamepad input API: auto , joystick or controller Font Options # Added by FontManager.args() in glitchygames/fonts/font_manager.py . Flag Type Default Description --font-name str arial Font name --font-size int 14 Font size in points --font-bold store_true False Bold font --font-italic store_true False Italic font --font-antialias store_true False Enable font antialiasing --font-dpi int 72 Font DPI --font-system choice freetype Font system: freetype (enhanced) or pygame (built-in) Reserved Groups (Empty, No Arguments Yet) # These groups exist as extension points. Each event manager creates its argument group but does not currently populate it with any flags. Group Name Source File Manager Class App Options events/app.py AppEventManager Sound Mixer Options events/audio.py AudioEventManager Drop Options events/drop.py DropEventManager Joystick Options events/joystick.py JoystickEventManager Keyboard Options events/keyboard.py KeyboardEventManager Midi Options events/midi.py MidiEventManager Mouse Options events/mouse.py MouseEventManager Touch Options events/touch.py TouchEventManager Window Options events/window.py WindowEventManager Synthetic Options (Not from argparse) # These are derived after parsing and injected into the OPTIONS dict. Key Type Derived From Description debug_events bool log_level Meant to be True for the debug , critical and error levels, but the code compares with upper-case names while --log-level is lower case, so it is always False (BUGS.md #74) Bitmappy Game-Specific Arguments # Added by BitmapEditorScene.args() in glitchygames/bitmappy/editor.py . These appear under the heading "Bitmappy vX.Y Options" in --help . Flag Type Default Description -v , --version store_true False Print the game version and exit -s , --size str 32x32 Canvas size (WxH in pixels) Example Game Arguments # Other games in the project demonstrate the pattern: Game File Arguments Paddle Slap glitchygames/examples/paddleslap.py -v, --version , -b, --balls (int, default 1), --ball-spawn-mode (choice, default paddle_only ) DT Demo glitchygames/examples/dt_demo.py -v, --version , -b, --balls (int, default 1) Clockwork Keep glitchygames/examples/clockwork_keep/game.py --floor (int, default 0) Brave Adventurer (both editions) glitchygames/examples/brave_adventurer/game.py , glitchygames/examples/brave_adventurer_papyrus/game.py -v, --version Joystick Demo glitchygames/examples/joystick_demo.py --time (int, default 10), -v, --version Bitrot Adventures scripts/bitrotadventures.py -s, --some-game-specific-option Animation Demo scripts/animation_scene_full_demo.py -v, --version What --help Looks Like # When a user runs uv run bitmappy --help , argparse produces output structured like this (argument groups appear in registration order): usage: Bitmappy version X.Y [-h] [-f TARGET_FPS] [...] options: -h, --help show this help message and exit Graphics Options: -f, --target-fps cap the framerate (default: the game's TARGET_FPS, else 60.01; 0 = uncapped) --fps-log-interval-ms how often to log the FPS counter in ms (default: 1000) -w, --windowed run the program in windowed mode -r, --resolution the resolution to use (default: 1024x768) --use-gfxdraw --update-type update or flip (default: update) --timer-backend timer backend for draw loop pacing (default: auto, the fast backend with this machine's sleep delay measured, so each sleep wakes in time; fast assumes sleeps wake on time; pygame is the legacy backend) --sleep-granularity-ns how long before each frame deadline the fast backend is to wake from its sleep and spin (ns); 0 spins only --windows-timer-1ms on Windows, request 1ms system timer resolution --random-seed master seed for every engine random stream (...) --screen-shake-intensity, --rumble-intensity, --live-voice-pool --video-driver Diagnostics Options: --log-timer-jitter log frame pacing jitter statistics periodically --perf-trim-percent percent of frames to trim from top and bottom in global FPS report --fps-histogram FPS histogram buckets in the shutdown report (...) --debug-overlay, --no-debug-overlay show the debug overlay at startup (F3 toggles, F4 cycles panels) --record-trace PATH record the session (...) --replay-trace PATH replay a --record-trace recording exactly (...) --replay-fps, --audit, --no-audit, --replay-digest PATH, --replay-pause-at-frame N (replay options) --headless run on SDL's dummy video and audio drivers: no window, no sound (...) App Options: Sound Mixer Options: Controller Options: --input-mode Gamepad input API (default: auto) Drop Options: Font Options: --font-name --font-size --font-bold --font-italic --font-antialias --font-dpi --font-system Font system to use: freetype (enhanced, default) or pygame (built-in) Game Options: -l, --log-level set the logging level --no-unhandled-events fail on unhandled events -p, --profile enable profiling Joystick Options: Keyboard Options: Midi Options: Mouse Options: Touch Options: Window Options: Bitmappy vX.Y Options: -v, --version print the game version and exit -s, --size The --resolution help text says 1024x768, but the default is 800x480 (BUGS.md #76). How to Add Arguments to a New Event Manager # If you are adding arguments to a currently-empty event manager group, follow the existing pattern: # In glitchygames/events/mouse.py @classmethod def args ( cls , parser : argparse . ArgumentParser ) -> argparse . ArgumentParser : group = parser . add_argument_group ( 'Mouse Options' ) group . add_argument ( '--mouse-sensitivity' , type = float , default = 1.0 , help = 'Mouse sensitivity multiplier (default: 1.0)' , ) return parser The engine already calls your manager's args() method — you just need to add add_argument() calls to the existing group. How to Create a New Game with Arguments # from glitchygames.engine import GameEngine from glitchygames.scenes import Scene class MyGame ( Scene ): NAME = 'My Game' VERSION = '1.0' @classmethod def args ( cls , parser ): """Add game-specific arguments. Args: parser: An argument group (not the root parser). """ parser . add_argument ( '-v' , '--version' , action = 'store_true' , help = 'print the game version and exit' , ) parser . add_argument ( '--difficulty' , choices = [ 'easy' , 'medium' , 'hard' ], default = 'medium' , help = 'game difficulty level' , ) def __init__ ( self , options ): super () . __init__ ( options = options ) # Access your arguments via self.options self . difficulty = self . options [ 'difficulty' ] def main (): GameEngine ( game = MyGame ) . start () Your arguments will automatically appear under "My Game v1.0 Options" in the --help output, separate from all engine-level flags.

Flag Type Default Description -f , --target-fps float None (the game's TARGET_FPS , else 60.01) Cap the framerate; 0 = uncapped --fps-log-interval-ms float 1000 How often to log the FPS counter in ms -w , --windowed store_true True Run in windowed mode (the default is already True , so the flag changes nothing) -r , --resolution str 800x480 Display resolution (WxH) --use-gfxdraw store_true False Use pygame.gfxdraw for rendering --update-type choice update Display update method: update or flip --timer-backend choice auto Timer backend: auto (the fast backend with this machine's sleep delay measured, so each sleep wakes in time), fast (assumes sleeps wake on time) or pygame (legacy) --sleep-granularity-ns int 1000000 How long before each frame deadline the fast backend is to wake from its sleep and spin (ns); 0 spins only --windows-timer-1ms store_true False On Windows, request 1ms system timer resolution --video-driver choice None Platform-specific video driver (see below) --random-seed int random 64-bit Master seed for every engine random stream --screen-shake-intensity float 1.0 Screen shake strength, 0.0 (off) to 1.0 --rumble-intensity float 1.0 Controller rumble strength, 0.0 (off) to 1.0 --live-voice-pool int 4 Mixer channels reserved for real-time synth voices --video-driver choices by platform: Platform Choices Linux wayland , x11 , dga , fbcon , directfb , ggi , vgl , svgalib , aalib Windows windib , directx macOS (none currently defined; the code checks platform.system() == 'MacOS' , which never matches, so macOS falls through to no choices either way)
docs.title: Graphics Options

docs.text: Added by GameEngine.args() right after the Graphics Options: how any run is watched, recorded, replayed or diagnosed, whatever the game. They change no game settings. Flag Type Default Description --log-timer-jitter store_true False Log frame pacing jitter statistics periodically --perf-trim-percent float 5.0 Percent of frames to trim from top and bottom in FPS report --fps-histogram choice equal-range FPS histogram buckets in the shutdown report: equal-range or target-relative --debug-overlay / --no-debug-overlay bool False Show the debug overlay at startup (F3 toggles, F4 cycles panels) --record-trace PATH None Record the session to a gzip JSON Lines trace ( Gameplay Recording and Replay ) --replay-trace PATH None Replay a recording exactly, reporting the first divergence --replay-fps choice None (read as recorded ) With --replay-trace : FPS events from the recorded or the real frame times --audit / --no-audit bool False With --replay-trace : replay twice in fresh processes and compare (exit 0, 3 when nondeterministic, 70 when a run could not finish; see exit codes ) --replay-digest PATH None With --replay-trace : write a SHA-256 per replayed frame (used by --audit ) --replay-pause-at-frame N (non-negative int) None With --replay-trace , watched: skip the start screen, rebuild frames 0 to N - 1 unpresented, then pause with frame N next (what step back restarts with; ignored with --headless ; step back ) --headless store_true False Run on SDL's dummy video and audio drivers (no window, no sound); a replay also runs unpaced and prints its report to stdout ( headless runs )

docs.text: When a user runs uv run bitmappy --help , argparse produces output structured like this (argument groups appear in registration order): usage: Bitmappy version X.Y [-h] [-f TARGET_FPS] [...] options: -h, --help show this help message and exit Graphics Options: -f, --target-fps cap the framerate (default: the game's TARGET_FPS, else 60.01; 0 = uncapped) --fps-log-interval-ms how often to log the FPS counter in ms (default: 1000) -w, --windowed run the program in windowed mode -r, --resolution the resolution to use (default: 1024x768) --use-gfxdraw --update-type update or flip (default: update) --timer-backend timer backend for draw loop pacing (default: auto, the fast backend with this machine's sleep delay measured, so each sleep wakes in time; fast assumes sleeps wake on time; pygame is the legacy backend) --sleep-granularity-ns how long before each frame deadline the fast backend is to wake from its sleep and spin (ns); 0 spins only --windows-timer-1ms on Windows, request 1ms system timer resolution --random-seed master seed for every engine random stream (...) --screen-shake-intensity, --rumble-intensity, --live-voice-pool --video-driver Diagnostics Options: --log-timer-jitter log frame pacing jitter statistics periodically --perf-trim-percent percent of frames to trim from top and bottom in global FPS report --fps-histogram FPS histogram buckets in the shutdown report (...) --debug-overlay, --no-debug-overlay show the debug overlay at startup (F3 toggles, F4 cycles panels) --record-trace PATH record the session (...) --replay-trace PATH replay a --record-trace recording exactly (...) --replay-fps, --audit, --no-audit, --replay-digest PATH, --replay-pause-at-frame N (replay options) --headless run on SDL's dummy video and audio drivers: no window, no sound (...) App Options: Sound Mixer Options: Controller Options: --input-mode Gamepad input API (default: auto) Drop Options: Font Options: --font-name --font-size --font-bold --font-italic --font-antialias --font-dpi --font-system Font system to use: freetype (enhanced, default) or pygame (built-in) Game Options: -l, --log-level set the logging level --no-unhandled-events fail on unhandled events -p, --profile enable profiling Joystick Options: Keyboard Options: Midi Options: Mouse Options: Touch Options: Window Options: Bitmappy vX.Y Options: -v, --version print the game version and exit -s, --size The --resolution help text says 1024x768, but the default is 800x480 (BUGS.md #76).

docs.text: If you are adding arguments to a currently-empty event manager group, follow the existing pattern: # In glitchygames/events/mouse.py @classmethod def args ( cls , parser : argparse . ArgumentParser ) -> argparse . ArgumentParser : group = parser . add_argument_group ( 'Mouse Options' ) group . add_argument ( '--mouse-sensitivity' , type = float , default = 1.0 , help = 'Mouse sensitivity multiplier (default: 1.0)' , ) return parser The engine already calls your manager's args() method — you just need to add add_argument() calls to the existing group.
docs.title: How to Add Arguments to a New Event Manager

docs.text: from glitchygames.engine import GameEngine from glitchygames.scenes import Scene class MyGame ( Scene ): NAME = 'My Game' VERSION = '1.0' @classmethod def args ( cls , parser ): """Add game-specific arguments. Args: parser: An argument group (not the root parser). """ parser . add_argument ( '-v' , '--version' , action = 'store_true' , help = 'print the game version and exit' , ) parser . add_argument ( '--difficulty' , choices = [ 'easy' , 'medium' , 'hard' ], default = 'medium' , help = 'game difficulty level' , ) def __init__ ( self , options ): super () . __init__ ( options = options ) # Access your arguments via self.options self . difficulty = self . options [ 'difficulty' ] def main (): GameEngine ( game = MyGame ) . start () Your arguments will automatically appear under "My Game v1.0 Options" in the --help output, separate from all engine-level flags.

Bitmappy Architecture # Bitmappy is GlitchyGames' pixel art editor. These diagrams show how it is wired up through the engine, from bootstrap to rendering. Bootstrap & Main Loop # How Bitmappy starts up: entry point through main() , GameEngine initialization, scene setup, and the main loop (one frame per pass, ended by _finish_frame ). sequenceDiagram participant User participant main as main() participant GE as GameEngine participant SM as SceneManager (singleton) participant BES as BitmapEditorScene User->>main: uv run bitmappy main->>GE: GameEngine(game=BitmapEditorScene) GE->>GE: parse CLI args (Scene.args() + GameEngine.args()) GE->>GE: pygame.init(), create display main->>GE: engine.start() GE->>BES: BitmapEditorScene(options=OPTIONS) GE->>GE: _initialize_event_managers() GE->>SM: scene_manager.switch_to_scene(game) SM->>BES: setup() BES->>BES: _setup_menu_bar() BES->>BES: _setup_canvas() BES->>BES: _create_film_strips() BES->>BES: _setup_color_well() BES->>BES: _setup_sliders() BES->>BES: _setup_managers() GE->>SM: scene_manager.start() loop Main Game Loop (while active_scene is not None) Note over SM: dt = the previous frame's start-to-start time SM->>SM: camera.begin_frame() SM->>BES: _update_scene() (Scene.dt_tick: logic and collision) SM->>GE: _process_events() GE->>GE: pygame.event.get() GE->>SM: EVENT_HANDLERS[event.type](event) SM->>BES: on_*_event(event) SM->>SM: _update_frame_services() (shake, rumble) SM->>SM: _aim_active_camera() (camera_target / follow) SM->>SM: _position_active_world_sprites() (world sprites' rect, culling) SM->>SM: _render_scene() (Scene.update, then draw) SM->>SM: _advance_still_camera_shake() (WORLD shake nothing advanced) SM->>SM: _present_frame() (overlay, display update) SM->>SM: _finish_frame() (pace, then set dt once from perf_counter) end Class Hierarchy # Event dispatch chain (how events reach your scene) # EventManager is the base class for GameEngine , SceneManager , and every Scene . This shared base is why events can flow through all of them using the same on_*_event() API. Inheritance — all dispatch chain classes share the EventManager base: flowchart LR EM["EventManager"] --- GE["GameEngine"] EM --- SM["SceneManager"] EM --- SC["Scene"] SC --- BES["BitmapEditorScene"] Event flow — how an SDL event reaches your handler in Bitmappy: flowchart TD SDL["SDL Event"] --> GE["GameEngine

forwards to active_scene"] SM --> BES["BitmapEditorScene

on_left_mouse_drag_event#40;#41;"] BES --> STUB["No handler?
Cached stub, O#40;1#41; no-op"] The GameEngine receives every SDL event and does an O(1) dict lookup to find the right event manager. The event manager updates its internal state (button tracking, axis values, drag detection) and may synthesize higher-level events (drag, drop, chord). It then forwards to the SceneManager , which passes everything to the active_scene . In Bitmappy, that's BitmapEditorScene , which overrides handlers like on_key_down_event() , on_left_mouse_button_down_event() , on_left_mouse_drag_event() , and on_controller_hat_motion_event() . Events it doesn't override hit the cached stubs — O(1) no-ops after their first occurrence.
