The header also holds what the run took in before recording started: a snapshot of every save store the doors opened (``saves``), the descriptors of devices opened (``devices``) and the enumeration answers given (``device_enumeration``). Then ``RecordingSources`` are installed around the active doors and record every frame from what passes through them (glitchygames/recording.py). SIGTERM (and SIGHUP on Unix, SIGBREAK on Windows) ends a started run through the normal teardown (``exit_on_signal``, installed by ``start``), and so does SIGINT (KeyboardInterrupt). ``stop_trace_recording`` (called by ``_shutdown``) closes the file. Recording must start before the first frame: afterwards installing its doors raises ``SourcesAlreadyRunningError`` (from ``install_sources``; glitchygames/sources.py). Args: path: The recording's file. Returns: The recorder. Raises: TraceRecordingAlreadyStartedError: If this engine is already recording. """ if self . trace_recorder is not None : message = ( f 'start_trace_recording() was called while recording to ' f ' { self . trace_recorder . path } ; one run records once' ) raise TraceRecordingAlreadyStartedError ( message ) inner = active_sources () registry = inner . devices () # A store a run started with --record-trace opened before recording started is in the # header as first opened: the first scene's setup() may have written to it since, and # the replay runs that setup() again (LiveSources.first_open_save_snapshots) first_open_snapshots : Mapping [ str , dict [ str , Any ]] = ( inner . first_open_save_snapshots if isinstance ( inner , LiveSources ) else {} ) # A rebaseline copies these fields from the replayed recording instead (rebaseline.py) header = { ** self . trace_recording_header (), SAVES_HEADER_FIELD : { namespace : ( first_open_snapshots [ namespace ] if namespace in first_open_snapshots else save_namespace_snapshot ( saves = store ) ) for namespace , store in inner . opened_save_namespaces . items () }, DEVICES_HEADER_FIELD : [ descriptor . to_json () for descriptor in registry . take_opened_descriptors () ], DEVICE_ENUMERATION_FIELD : [ answer . to_json () for answer in registry . take_enumeration_answers () ], } recorder = GameplayRecorder ( path = path , header = header ) install_sources ( sources = RecordingSources ( inner = inner , recorder = recorder )) self . trace_recorder = recorder self . log . info ( f 'Recording gameplay to { path } (random seed { self . random_seed } )' ) return recorder

docs.text: Override the default subclasshook to create an interface. A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass even without inheriting from it. Per the abc contract, anything else returns NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods, so the structural check never passes for it). Returns: bool ( bool ) – True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented (typeshed annotates object. subclasshook as bool and types NotImplemented as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides. Source code in glitchygames/events/base.py 555 556 557 558 559 560 561 562 563 564 565 566 567 568 569 570 571 572 573 574 575 576 577 578 579 580 581 582 583 584 585 586 587 588 589 590 591 592 593 594 595 596 597 598 599 @classmethod @override def __subclasshook__ ( cls , subclass : type [ Any ]) -> bool : """Override the default __subclasshook__ to create an interface. A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass even without inheriting from it. Per the `abc` contract, anything else returns NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods, so the structural check never passes for it). Returns: bool: True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented (typeshed annotates object.__subclasshook__ as bool and types NotImplemented as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides. """ # Note: This accounts for under/dunder methods in addition to regular methods. interface_attributes = set ( cls . __abstractmethods__ ) abstract_methods = getattr ( subclass , '__abstractmethods__' , frozenset [ str ]()) subclass_attributes : set [ str ] = set ( abstract_methods ) interface_is_implemented = False methods : list [ bool ] = [] for attribute in sorted ( interface_attributes ): if hasattr ( subclass , attribute ) and attribute not in subclass_attributes : if callable ( getattr ( subclass , attribute )): cls . log . debug ( f ' { subclass . __name__ } . { attribute } -> implemented (callable)' ) else : cls . log . debug ( f ' { subclass . __name__ } . { attribute } -> implemented (attribute)' ) methods . append ( True ) else : cls . log . debug ( f ' { subclass . __name__ } . { attribute } -> unimplemented' ) methods . append ( False ) # all([]) returns True, so mask it # # This protects against an empty attribute list # which would be a misconfiguration of the interface if len ( methods ) > 0 and all ( methods ): interface_is_implemented = all ( methods ) if interface_is_implemented : return True return NotImplemented

docs.text: End the run with SystemExit, so GameEngine.start()'s teardown still runs. Installed by GameEngine.start for each of terminating_signals() that nothing else handles, for the whole run, so a recording is closed by _shutdown . It ignores further signals of the same kind before raising: a second SIGTERM ( uv run forwards one to its child as well, and pkill can match both) would otherwise raise again inside the teardown and leave the recording unclosed. _shutdown restores the default handling after closing the recording. It does nothing else: logging here could fail with "reentrant call" if the signal interrupted a write to the same stream. Parameters: signal_number ( int ) – The signal received. _frame ( FrameType | None ) – The interrupted frame (unused). Raises: SystemExit – Always, with ExitCode.for_signal(signal_number) ( TERMINATED for SIGTERM, HANGUP for SIGHUP, BREAK for SIGBREAK). Source code in glitchygames/engine/game_engine.py 266 267 268 269 270 271 272 273 274 275 276 277 278 279 280 281 282 283 284 285 286 287 def exit_on_signal ( signal_number : int , _frame : FrameType | None ) -> None : """End the run with SystemExit, so GameEngine.start()'s teardown still runs. Installed by ``GameEngine.start`` for each of ``terminating_signals()`` that nothing else handles, for the whole run, so a recording is closed by ``_shutdown``. It ignores further signals of the same kind before raising: a second SIGTERM (``uv run`` forwards one to its child as well, and ``pkill`` can match both) would otherwise raise again inside the teardown and leave the recording unclosed. ``_shutdown`` restores the default handling after closing the recording. It does nothing else: logging here could fail with "reentrant call" if the signal interrupted a write to the same stream. Args: signal_number: The signal received. _frame: The interrupted frame (unused). Raises: SystemExit: Always, with ``ExitCode.for_signal(signal_number)`` (``TERMINATED`` for SIGTERM, ``HANGUP`` for SIGHUP, ``BREAK`` for SIGBREAK). """ signal . signal ( signal_number , signal . SIG_IGN ) raise SystemExit ( ExitCode . for_signal ( signal_number ))

Source code in glitchygames/exit_codes.py 82 83 84 85 86 87 88 89 90 91 92 93 94 95 96 97 98 99 100 101 102 103 104 105 106 107 108 109 110 111 112 113 114 115 116 117 118 119 120 121 122 123 124 125 126 127 128 129 130 131 132 133 134 135 136 137 138 139 140 141 142 143 144 145 146 147 148 149 150 151 152 153 154 155 156 157 158 159 160 161 162 163 164 165 166 167 168 169 170 171 172 173 174 175 176 177 178 179 180 181 182 183 184 185 186 187 188 189 190 191 192 193 194 195 196 197 198 199 200 201 202 203 204 205 206 207 208 209 210 211 212 213 class ExitCode ( enum . IntEnum ): """The process exit codes of the engine, the replay tools and the API client.""" # Success; the replay matched; the audit is deterministic. Same value as Python's os.EX_OK # (sysexits.h EX_OK) SUCCESS = 0 # A replay's frames differ from the recording REPLAY_DIVERGED = 1 # argparse's own status for a usage error. The engine never exits with it: it is named for # callers and tests that tell argparse's refusals from the engine's ARGUMENT_PARSER_ERROR = 2 # --audit's two replay runs differ from each other or from the recording AUDIT_NONDETERMINISTIC = 3 # The API server rejected the client's sprite generation (an error status, or a response that # says it failed) GENERATION_REJECTED = 4 # The API server rejected the client's frame extraction (an error status, or a response that # says it failed) EXTRACTION_REJECTED = 5 # scripts/audio_glitch_probe.py found a risk of audio dropouts AUDIO_DROPOUT_RISK = 6 # --rebaseline wrote the new recording, but the run never received some of the old one's # input (glitchygames/replay/rebaseline.py, rule 2) REBASELINE_INPUT_LOST = 7 # A replay matched, but took longer to process than --max-processing-slowdown allows; see # glitchygames/replay/processing.py PROCESSING_SLOWER = 8 # The engine refuses the options given (a combination it will not run). Same value as # Python's os.EX_USAGE (sysexits.h EX_USAGE) OPTIONS_REFUSED = 64 # The recording or input data is unusable. Same value as Python's os.EX_DATAERR (sysexits.h # EX_DATAERR) UNUSABLE_INPUT = 65 # The input file does not exist. Same value as Python's os.EX_NOINPUT (sysexits.h EX_NOINPUT) MISSING_INPUT = 66 # A required service (the API server) cannot be reached. Same value as Python's # os.EX_UNAVAILABLE (sysexits.h EX_UNAVAILABLE) SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE = 69 # An uncaught exception during a run, or an audit that could not run. Same value as Python's # os.EX_SOFTWARE (sysexits.h EX_SOFTWARE) INTERNAL_ERROR = 70 # An output file or directory cannot be created or written. Same value as Python's # os.EX_CANTCREAT (sysexits.h EX_CANTCREAT) CANNOT_WRITE_OUTPUT = 73 # Stopped by SIGHUP (Unix only): 128 + signal.SIGHUP HANGUP = 129 # Stopped by SIGINT (Ctrl-C): 128 + signal.SIGINT INTERRUPTED = 130 # Stopped by SIGTERM: 128 + signal.SIGTERM TERMINATED = 143 # Stopped by SIGBREAK (Windows only: Ctrl-Break): 128 + signal.SIGBREAK BREAK = 149 @classmethod def for_signal ( cls , signal_number : int ) -> ExitCode : """Return the member a run stopped by a signal exits with. Args: signal_number: The signal (``signal.SIGTERM`` and so on). Returns: ``HANGUP``, ``INTERRUPTED``, ``TERMINATED`` or ``BREAK``. Raises: ValueError: For a signal the engine does not wire (see the module docstring), rather than a number with no name. """ message = f 'signal { signal_number } has no exit code: the engine does not handle it' if signal_number <= 0 : raise ValueError ( message ) try : return cls ( SIGNAL_EXIT_STATUS_BASE + signal_number ) except ValueError as error : raise ValueError ( message ) from error def describe ( self ) -> str : """Return the code's name and number, as logs show it. ``str()`` of an IntEnum member is only its number (Python 3.11 on). Returns: For example ``'OPTIONS_REFUSED (64)'``. """ return f ' { self . name } ( { self . value } )' @classmethod def describe_status ( cls , status : int ) -> str : """Describe any process exit status: a member, a signal exit, or an unknown number. Args: status: A process's exit status (a child's ``returncode``). Returns: ``'INTERNAL_ERROR (70)'`` for a member; for a signal, ``'signal 6 (134)'`` (128 + the signal number, as a shell reports it) or, for a process killed by the signal (a subprocess reports -N), ``'TERMINATED (signal 15)'`` where the signal has a member and ``'signal 6'`` otherwise; any other number alone. """ if status < 0 : signal_number = - status try : return f ' { cls . for_signal ( signal_number ) . name } (signal { signal_number } )' except ValueError : return f 'signal { signal_number } ' try : return cls ( status ) . describe () except ValueError : pass if status > SIGNAL_EXIT_STATUS_BASE : return f 'signal { status - SIGNAL_EXIT_STATUS_BASE } ( { status } )' return str ( status )

docs.text: Process every event queued this frame. pygame.event.get() removes the whole batch from SDL's queue at once, so every event of the batch is handled here: none may be dropped. Each event is judged on its own; an event whose type has no entry in EVENT_HANDLERS , or whose handler did not handle it, goes to process_unimplemented_event . Parameters: should_discard ( Callable [[ Event ], bool ] | None , default: None ) – Returns True for an event to remove from the batch without processing it (not counted as unhandled). SceneManager passes is_discarded_during_transition during a transition. Returns: bool ( bool ) – True if at least one event was dispatched and every dispatched event was bool – handled (a raw-event scene's process_event counts as handled). False if any bool – dispatched event was unhandled, or if nothing was dispatched: an empty batch, or bool – one whose events were all discarded. Event ], bool ] | None = None ) -> bool : """Process every event queued this frame. ``pygame.event.get()`` removes the whole batch from SDL's queue at once, so every event of the batch is handled here: none may be dropped. Each event is judged on its own; an event whose type has no entry in ``EVENT_HANDLERS``, or whose handler did not handle it, goes to ``process_unimplemented_event``. Args: should_discard: Returns True for an event to remove from the batch without processing it (not counted as unhandled). SceneManager passes ``is_discarded_during_transition`` during a transition. Returns: bool: True if at least one event was dispatched and every dispatched event was handled (a raw-event scene's ``process_event`` counts as handled). False if any dispatched event was unhandled, or if nothing was dispatched: an empty batch, or one whose events were all discarded. """ raw_events = self . _pump_events () # Polled input is read once per frame, right after the pump, so it agrees with this # frame's events; it stays fixed until the next frame's pump, so dt_tick (which runs # before this) reads the previous frame's snapshot (glitchygames/input/state.py) set_current_input ( snapshot = active_sources () . input_snapshot ()) dispatched_event_count = 0 every_event_was_handled = True for pygame_event in raw_events : if should_discard is not None and should_discard ( pygame_event ): continue dispatched_event_count += 1 # Support scenes processing pygame raw events, bypassing # the glitchygames.engine event processing altogether if hasattr ( self . _active_scene , 'process_event' ): self . _active_scene . process_event ( pygame_event ) # type: ignore[union-attr] # ty: ignore[call-non-callable] continue event : events . HashableEvent = events . HashableEvent ( type = pygame_event . type ) event . __dict__ . update ( pygame_event . dict ) # Decided per event: a type missing from the map is unhandled event_was_handled = False if event . type in GameEngine . EVENT_HANDLERS : event_was_handled = bool ( GameEngine . EVENT_HANDLERS [ event . type ]( event )) # If an event is not in the event handler map, or the function # called didn't handle the event in question, we'll process it # as an unimplemented event if not event_was_handled : self . process_unimplemented_event ( event ) every_event_was_handled = False return dispatched_event_count > 0 and every_event_was_handled

Returns: float ( float ) – The effective target FPS (0 means uncapped). Raises: TypeError – If the game's TARGET_FPS is neither None nor a (non-bool) number. Order: explicit command line value (0 = uncapped) > the game's TARGET_FPS (when not None) > DEFAULT_TARGET_FPS. Args: command_line_target_fps: The --target-fps value, or None if it was not passed. game: The game scene class or instance, which may declare TARGET_FPS. Returns: float: The effective target FPS (0 means uncapped). Raises: TypeError: If the game's TARGET_FPS is neither None nor a (non-bool) number. ValueError: If the game's TARGET_FPS is negative, NaN or infinite. """ if command_line_target_fps is not None : return float ( command_line_target_fps ) game_target_fps = getattr ( game , 'TARGET_FPS' , None ) if game_target_fps is None : return DEFAULT_TARGET_FPS scene_class = game if isinstance ( game , type ) else type ( game ) # bool is a subclass of int, so it must be rejected explicitly. if isinstance ( game_target_fps , bool ) or not isinstance ( game_target_fps , ( int , float )): message = ( f ' { scene_class . __name__ } .TARGET_FPS must be a number or None, ' f 'got { game_target_fps !r} ' ) raise TypeError ( message ) if not math . isfinite ( game_target_fps ) or game_target_fps < 0 : message = ( f ' { scene_class . __name__ } .TARGET_FPS must be a finite number >= 0 ' f '(0 = uncapped), got { game_target_fps !r} ' ) raise ValueError ( message ) return float ( game_target_fps )

docs.text: Start the game engine. However the run ends, the teardown ( _shutdown : recordings closed) runs first; if the teardown itself raises, the run exits ExitCode.INTERNAL_ERROR (both errors logged). An exception raised before start(), in __init__ , is not mapped: it exits with Python's default 1 (each game has its own entry point, so there is no one place to wrap; see glitchygames/exit_codes.py). A replay ( --replay-trace ) that ends normally exits with its own code ( ReplayResult.exit_code under its exit policy), watched or headless. Raises: RuntimeError – If the game is not initialized. SystemExit – With ExitCode.INTERNAL_ERROR after an uncaught exception (logged with its traceback), ExitCode.INTERRUPTED after Ctrl-C (KeyboardInterrupt), or whatever status a SystemExit raised during the run carries (a signal handler's, a game's own), except a game's own successful exit that cuts a replay short ( ExitCode.REPLAY_DIVERGED ; a rebaseline ends normally then, with what the game ran); at the normal end of a replay, with the replay's exit code ( ExitCode.SUCCESS , ExitCode.REPLAY_DIVERGED or ExitCode.UNUSABLE_INPUT for a truncated recording). Source code in glitchygames/engine/game_engine.py 2184 2185 2186 2187 2188 2189 2190 2191 2192 2193 2194 2195 2196 2197 2198 2199 2200 2201 2202 2203 2204 2205 2206 2207 2208 2209 2210 2211 2212 2213 2214 2215 2216 2217 2218 2219 2220 2221 2222 2223 2224 2225 2226 2227 2228 2229 2230 2231 2232 2233 2234 2235 2236 2237 2238 2239 2240 2241 2242 2243 2244 2245 2246 2247 2248 2249 2250 2251 2252 2253 def start ( self : Self ) -> None : """Start the game engine. However the run ends, the teardown (``_shutdown``: recordings closed) runs first; if the teardown itself raises, the run exits ``ExitCode.INTERNAL_ERROR`` (both errors logged). An exception raised before start(), in ``__init__``, is not mapped: it exits with Python's default 1 (each game has its own entry point, so there is no one place to wrap; see glitchygames/exit_codes.py). A replay (``--replay-trace``) that ends normally exits with its own code (``ReplayResult.exit_code`` under its exit policy), watched or headless. Raises: RuntimeError: If the game is not initialized. SystemExit: With ``ExitCode.INTERNAL_ERROR`` after an uncaught exception (logged with its traceback), ``ExitCode.INTERRUPTED`` after Ctrl-C (KeyboardInterrupt), or whatever status a SystemExit raised during the run carries (a signal handler's, a game's own), except a game's own successful exit that cuts a replay short (``ExitCode.REPLAY_DIVERGED``; a rebaseline ends normally then, with what the game ran); at the normal end of a replay, with the replay's exit code (``ExitCode.SUCCESS``, ``ExitCode.REPLAY_DIVERGED`` or ``ExitCode.UNUSABLE_INPUT`` for a truncated recording). """ # This ensures that logging is enabled as soon as the game object is created. logging . getLogger ( 'game' ) self . log . info ( f 'Starting game engine for game: { type ( self ) . NAME } ' ) if self . game is None : raise RuntimeError ( GAME_NOT_INITIALIZED_MSG ) profiler = None if GameEngine . OPTIONS [ 'profile' ]: # Enabled before the crash boundary, so the teardown prints only a profiler that ran profiler = cProfile . Profile () profiler . enable () # Set when the run ends in a way that start() turns into an exit code exit_code : ExitCode | None = None run_error : Exception | None = None # What ended the run early, described for the replay report (None: a normal end) run_ended_by : str | None = None try : # The crash boundary: anything the run raises is turned into an exit code below self . _run_game () except KeyboardInterrupt : # Ctrl-C: never an internal error; exits INTERRUPTED once the teardown has run exit_code = ExitCode . INTERRUPTED run_ended_by = exit_code . describe () except SystemExit as exit_request : # A deliberate exit (a signal handler's, a game's) keeps its status run_ended_by = self . _describe_exit_request ( exit_status = exit_request . code ) if not self . _exit_cuts_a_replay_short ( exit_status = exit_request . code ): raise exit_code , run_ended_by = self . _outcome_of_a_replay_cut_short ( run_ended_by = run_ended_by ) except RecordingWriteError as error : # The disk filled part way: logged on one line by the recorder (BUGS.md #82) exit_code = ExitCode . CANNOT_WRITE_OUTPUT run_ended_by = exit_code . describe () run_error = error except Exception as error : scene_name = self . _resolve_scene_name_for_error () self . log . exception ( "Runtime error during game execution @ scene ' %s '" , scene_name ) exit_code = ExitCode . INTERNAL_ERROR run_ended_by = exit_code . describe () run_error = error finally : teardown_error = self . _tear_down_run ( profiler = profiler , run_ended_by = run_ended_by ) if teardown_error is not None : # Replaces whatever was ending the run: a failed teardown is an internal error exit_with ( exit_code = ExitCode . INTERNAL_ERROR , cause = teardown_error ) self . _end_run ( exit_code = exit_code , run_error = run_error )

docs.text: Start recording the session to a trace file (before the first frame). The header also holds what the run took in before recording started: a snapshot of every save store the doors opened ( saves ), the descriptors of devices opened ( devices ) and the enumeration answers given ( device_enumeration ). Then RecordingSources are installed around the active doors and record every frame from what passes through them (glitchygames/recording.py). SIGTERM (and SIGHUP on Unix, SIGBREAK on Windows) ends a started run through the normal teardown ( exit_on_signal , installed by start ), and so does SIGINT (KeyboardInterrupt). stop_trace_recording (called by _shutdown ) closes the file. Recording must start before the first frame: afterwards installing its doors raises SourcesAlreadyRunningError (from install_sources ; glitchygames/sources.py). Parameters: path ( Path ) – The recording's file. Returns: GameplayRecorder – The recorder. Raises: TraceRecordingAlreadyStartedError – If this engine is already recording. Source code in glitchygames/engine/game_engine.py 1558 1559 1560 1561 1562 1563 1564 1565 1566 1567 1568 1569 1570 1571 1572 1573 1574 1575 1576 1577 1578 1579 1580 1581 1582 1583 1584 1585 1586 1587 1588 1589 1590 1591 1592 1593 1594 1595 1596 1597 1598 1599 1600 1601 1602 1603 1604 1605 1606 1607 1608 1609 1610 1611 1612 1613 1614 1615 1616 1617 1618 1619 def start_trace_recording ( self : Self , * , path : Path ) -> GameplayRecorder : """Start recording the session to a trace file (before the first frame). The header also holds what the run took in before recording started: a snapshot of every save store the doors opened (``saves``), the descriptors of devices opened (``devices``) and the enumeration answers given (``device_enumeration``). Then ``RecordingSources`` are installed around the active doors and record every frame from what passes through them (glitchygames/recording.py). SIGTERM (and SIGHUP on Unix, SIGBREAK on Windows) ends a started run through the normal teardown (``exit_on_signal``, installed by ``start``), and so does SIGINT (KeyboardInterrupt). ``stop_trace_recording`` (called by ``_shutdown``) closes the file. Recording must start before the first frame: afterwards installing its doors raises ``SourcesAlreadyRunningError`` (from ``install_sources``; glitchygames/sources.py). Args: path: The recording's file. Returns: The recorder. Raises: TraceRecordingAlreadyStartedError: If this engine is already recording. """ if self . trace_recorder is not None : message = ( f 'start_trace_recording() was called while recording to ' f ' { self . trace_recorder . path } ; one run records once' ) raise TraceRecordingAlreadyStartedError ( message ) inner = active_sources () registry = inner . devices () # A store a run started with --record-trace opened before recording started is in the # header as first opened: the first scene's setup() may have written to it since, and # the replay runs that setup() again (LiveSources.first_open_save_snapshots) first_open_snapshots : Mapping [ str , dict [ str , Any ]] = ( inner . first_open_save_snapshots if isinstance ( inner , LiveSources ) else {} ) # A rebaseline copies these fields from the replayed recording instead (rebaseline.py) header = { ** self . trace_recording_header (), SAVES_HEADER_FIELD : { namespace : ( first_open_snapshots [ namespace ] if namespace in first_open_snapshots else save_namespace_snapshot ( saves = store ) ) for namespace , store in inner . opened_save_namespaces . items () }, DEVICES_HEADER_FIELD : [ descriptor . to_json () for descriptor in registry . take_opened_descriptors () ], DEVICE_ENUMERATION_FIELD : [ answer . to_json () for answer in registry . take_enumeration_answers () ], } recorder = GameplayRecorder ( path = path , header = header ) install_sources ( sources = RecordingSources ( inner = inner , recorder = recorder )) self . trace_recorder = recorder self . log . info ( f 'Recording gameplay to { path } (random seed { self . random_seed } )' ) return recorder

The ``RecordingSources`` stay installed (the run is ending); with the recorder closed they only delegate. docs.text: Describe every unhandled event type, most frequent first. Each line names the type (pygame's event name and its number, so custom and unknown types still show), its count, when it was first seen and the first event's attribute names, e.g. JOYDEVICEADDED (1541) x1, first at 0.3 s, attributes: device_index, guid . Returns: list [ str ] – One line per type; empty when every event was handled. Source code in glitchygames/engine/game_engine.py 3129 3130 3131 3132 3133 3134 3135 3136 3137 3138 3139 3140 3141 3142 3143 3144 3145 3146 3147 3148 3149 3150 def unhandled_event_report ( self : Self ) -> list [ str ]: """Describe every unhandled event type, most frequent first. Returns: One line per type; empty when every event was handled. docs.text: Override the default subclasshook to create an interface. A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass even without inheriting from it. Per the abc contract, anything else returns NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods, so the structural check never passes for it). Returns: bool ( bool ) – True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented (typeshed annotates object. subclasshook as bool and types NotImplemented as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides. Source code in glitchygames/events/base.py 555 556 557 558 559 560 561 562 563 564 565 566 567 568 569 570 571 572 573 574 575 576 577 578 579 580 581 582 583 584 585 586 587 588 589 590 591 592 593 594 595 596 597 598 599 @classmethod @override def __subclasshook__ ( cls , subclass : type [ Any ]) -> bool : """Override the default __subclasshook__ to create an interface. A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass even without inheriting from it. Per the `abc` contract, anything else returns NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods, so the structural check never passes for it). Returns: bool: True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented (typeshed annotates object.__subclasshook__ as bool and types NotImplemented as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides. """ # Note: This accounts for under/dunder methods in addition to regular methods. interface_attributes = set ( cls . __abstractmethods__ ) abstract_methods = getattr ( subclass , '__abstractmethods__' , frozenset [ str ]()) subclass_attributes : set [ str ] = set ( abstract_methods ) interface_is_implemented = False methods : list [ bool ] = [] for attribute in sorted ( interface_attributes ): if hasattr ( subclass , attribute ) and attribute not in subclass_attributes : if callable ( getattr ( subclass , attribute )): cls . log . debug ( f ' { subclass . __name__ } . { attribute } -> implemented (callable)' ) else : cls . log . debug ( f ' { subclass . __name__ } . { attribute } -> implemented (attribute)' ) methods . append ( True ) else : cls . log . debug ( f ' { subclass . __name__ } . { attribute } -> unimplemented' ) methods . append ( False ) # all([]) returns True, so mask it # # This protects against an empty attribute list # which would be a misconfiguration of the interface if len ( methods ) > 0 and all ( methods ): interface_is_implemented = all ( methods ) if interface_is_implemented : return True return NotImplemented

docs.text: End the run with SystemExit, so GameEngine.start()'s teardown still runs. Installed by GameEngine.start for each of terminating_signals() that nothing else handles, for the whole run, so a recording is closed by _shutdown . It ignores further signals of the same kind before raising: a second SIGTERM ( uv run forwards one to its child as well, and pkill can match both) would otherwise raise again inside the teardown and leave the recording unclosed. _shutdown restores the default handling after closing the recording. It does nothing else: logging here could fail with "reentrant call" if the signal interrupted a write to the same stream. Parameters: signal_number ( int ) – The signal received. _frame ( FrameType | None ) – The interrupted frame (unused). Raises: SystemExit – Always, with ExitCode.for_signal(signal_number) ( TERMINATED for SIGTERM, HANGUP for SIGHUP, BREAK for SIGBREAK). Source code in glitchygames/engine/game_engine.py 266 267 268 269 270 271 272 273 274 275 276 277 278 279 280 281 282 283 284 285 286 287 def exit_on_signal ( signal_number : int , _frame : FrameType | None ) -> None : """End the run with SystemExit, so GameEngine.start()'s teardown still runs. Installed by ``GameEngine.start`` for each of ``terminating_signals()`` that nothing else handles, for the whole run, so a recording is closed by ``_shutdown``. It ignores further signals of the same kind before raising: a second SIGTERM (``uv run`` forwards one to its child as well, and ``pkill`` can match both) would otherwise raise again inside the teardown and leave the recording unclosed. ``_shutdown`` restores the default handling after closing the recording. It does nothing else: logging here could fail with "reentrant call" if the signal interrupted a write to the same stream. Args: signal_number: The signal received. _frame: The interrupted frame (unused). Raises: SystemExit: Always, with ``ExitCode.for_signal(signal_number)`` (``TERMINATED`` for SIGTERM, ``HANGUP`` for SIGHUP, ``BREAK`` for SIGBREAK). """ signal . signal ( signal_number , signal . SIG_IGN ) raise SystemExit ( ExitCode . for_signal ( signal_number ))

Source code in glitchygames/exit_codes.py 82 83 84 85 86 87 88 89 90 91 92 93 94 95 96 97 98 99 100 101 102 103 104 105 106 107 108 109 110 111 112 113 114 115 116 117 118 119 120 121 122 123 124 125 126 127 128 129 130 131 132 133 134 135 136 137 138 139 140 141 142 143 144 145 146 147 148 149 150 151 152 153 154 155 156 157 158 159 160 161 162 163 164 165 166 167 168 169 170 171 172 173 174 175 176 177 178 179 180 181 182 183 184 185 186 187 188 189 190 191 192 193 194 195 196 197 198 199 200 201 202 203 204 205 206 207 208 209 210 211 212 213 class ExitCode ( enum . IntEnum ): """The process exit codes of the engine, the replay tools and the API client.""" # Success; the replay matched; the audit is deterministic. Same value as Python's os.EX_OK # (sysexits.h EX_OK) SUCCESS = 0 # A replay's frames differ from the recording REPLAY_DIVERGED = 1 # argparse's own status for a usage error. The engine never exits with it: it is named for # callers and tests that tell argparse's refusals from the engine's ARGUMENT_PARSER_ERROR = 2 # --audit's two replay runs differ from each other or from the recording AUDIT_NONDETERMINISTIC = 3 # The API server rejected the client's sprite generation (an error status, or a response that # says it failed) GENERATION_REJECTED = 4 # The API server rejected the client's frame extraction (an error status, or a response that # says it failed) EXTRACTION_REJECTED = 5 # scripts/audio_glitch_probe.py found a risk of audio dropouts AUDIO_DROPOUT_RISK = 6 # --rebaseline wrote the new recording, but the run never received some of the old one's # input (glitchygames/replay/rebaseline.py, rule 2) REBASELINE_INPUT_LOST = 7 # A replay matched, but took longer to process than --max-processing-slowdown allows; see # glitchygames/replay/processing.py PROCESSING_SLOWER = 8 # The engine refuses the options given (a combination it will not run). Same value as # Python's os.EX_USAGE (sysexits.h EX_USAGE) OPTIONS_REFUSED = 64 # The recording or input data is unusable. Same value as Python's os.EX_DATAERR (sysexits.h # EX_DATAERR) UNUSABLE_INPUT = 65 # The input file does not exist. Same value as Python's os.EX_NOINPUT (sysexits.h EX_NOINPUT) MISSING_INPUT = 66 # A required service (the API server) cannot be reached. Same value as Python's # os.EX_UNAVAILABLE (sysexits.h EX_UNAVAILABLE) SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE = 69 # An uncaught exception during a run, or an audit that could not run. Same value as Python's # os.EX_SOFTWARE (sysexits.h EX_SOFTWARE) INTERNAL_ERROR = 70 # An output file or directory cannot be created or written. Same value as Python's # os.EX_CANTCREAT (sysexits.h EX_CANTCREAT) CANNOT_WRITE_OUTPUT = 73 # Stopped by SIGHUP (Unix only): 128 + signal.SIGHUP HANGUP = 129 # Stopped by SIGINT (Ctrl-C): 128 + signal.SIGINT INTERRUPTED = 130 # Stopped by SIGTERM: 128 + signal.SIGTERM TERMINATED = 143 # Stopped by SIGBREAK (Windows only: Ctrl-Break): 128 + signal.SIGBREAK BREAK = 149 @classmethod def for_signal ( cls , signal_number : int ) -> ExitCode : """Return the member a run stopped by a signal exits with. Args: signal_number: The signal (``signal.SIGTERM`` and so on). Returns: ``HANGUP``, ``INTERRUPTED``, ``TERMINATED`` or ``BREAK``. Raises: ValueError: For a signal the engine does not wire (see the module docstring), rather than a number with no name. """ message = f 'signal { signal_number } has no exit code: the engine does not handle it' if signal_number <= 0 : raise ValueError ( message ) try : return cls ( SIGNAL_EXIT_STATUS_BASE + signal_number ) except ValueError as error : raise ValueError ( message ) from error def describe ( self ) -> str : """Return the code's name and number, as logs show it. ``str()`` of an IntEnum member is only its number (Python 3.11 on). Returns: For example ``'OPTIONS_REFUSED (64)'``. """ return f ' { self . name } ( { self . value } )' @classmethod def describe_status ( cls , status : int ) -> str : """Describe any process exit status: a member, a signal exit, or an unknown number. Args: status: A process's exit status (a child's ``returncode``). Returns: ``'INTERNAL_ERROR (70)'`` for a member; for a signal, ``'signal 6 (134)'`` (128 + the signal number, as a shell reports it) or, for a process killed by the signal (a subprocess reports -N), ``'TERMINATED (signal 15)'`` where the signal has a member and ``'signal 6'`` otherwise; any other number alone. """ if status < 0 : signal_number = - status try : return f ' { cls . for_signal ( signal_number ) . name } (signal { signal_number } )' except ValueError : return f 'signal { signal_number } ' try : return cls ( status ) . describe () except ValueError : pass if status > SIGNAL_EXIT_STATUS_BASE : return f 'signal { status - SIGNAL_EXIT_STATUS_BASE } ( { status } )' return str ( status )

docs.text: Initialize event handlers. The engine calls this on your behalf. Event subsystem bootstrapping This gives us much faster event processing than doing a lookup every time an event comes in since we can just call the processing function directly. docs.text: Process every event queued this frame. pygame.event.get() removes the whole batch from SDL's queue at once, so every event of the batch is handled here: none may be dropped. Each event is judged on its own; an event whose type has no entry in EVENT_HANDLERS , or whose handler did not handle it, goes to process_unimplemented_event . Parameters: should_discard ( Callable [[ Event ], bool ] | None , default: None ) – Returns True for an event to remove from the batch without processing it (not counted as unhandled). SceneManager passes is_discarded_during_transition during a transition. Returns: bool ( bool ) – True if at least one event was dispatched and every dispatched event was bool – handled (a raw-event scene's process_event counts as handled). False if any bool – dispatched event was unhandled, or if nothing was dispatched: an empty batch, or bool – one whose events were all discarded. Source code in glitchygames/engine/game_engine.py 2501 2502 2503 2504 2505 2506 2507 2508 2509 2510 2511 2512 2513 2514 2515 2516 2517 2518 2519 2520 2521 2522 2523 2524 2525 2526 2527 2528 2529 2530 2531 2532 2533 2534 2535 2536 2537 2538 2539 2540 2541 2542 2543 2544 2545 2546 2547 2548 2549 2550 2551 2552 2553 2554 2555 2556 def process_events ( self : Self , * , should_discard : Callable [[ pygame . event . Event ], bool ] | None = None ) -> bool : """Process every event queued this frame. ``pygame.event.get()`` removes the whole batch from SDL's queue at once, so every event of the batch is handled here: none may be dropped. Each event is judged on its own; an event whose type has no entry in ``EVENT_HANDLERS``, or whose handler did not handle it, goes to ``process_unimplemented_event``. Args: should_discard: Returns True for an event to remove from the batch without processing it (not counted as unhandled). SceneManager passes ``is_discarded_during_transition`` during a transition. Returns: bool: True if at least one event was dispatched and every dispatched event was handled (a raw-event scene's ``process_event`` counts as handled). False if any dispatched event was unhandled, or if nothing was dispatched: an empty batch, or one whose events were all discarded. """ raw_events = self . _pump_events () # Polled input is read once per frame, right after the pump, so it agrees with this # frame's events; it stays fixed until the next frame's pump, so dt_tick (which runs # before this) reads the previous frame's snapshot (glitchygames/input/state.py) set_current_input ( snapshot = active_sources () . input_snapshot ()) dispatched_event_count = 0 every_event_was_handled = True for pygame_event in raw_events : if should_discard is not None and should_discard ( pygame_event ): continue dispatched_event_count += 1 # Support scenes processing pygame raw events, bypassing # the glitchygames.engine event processing altogether if hasattr ( self . _active_scene , 'process_event' ): self . _active_scene . process_event ( pygame_event ) # type: ignore[union-attr] # ty: ignore[call-non-callable] continue event : events . HashableEvent = events . HashableEvent ( type = pygame_event . type ) event . __dict__ . update ( pygame_event . dict ) # Decided per event: a type missing from the map is unhandled event_was_handled = False if event . type in GameEngine . EVENT_HANDLERS : event_was_handled = bool ( GameEngine . EVENT_HANDLERS [ event . type ]( event )) # If an event is not in the event handler map, or the function # called didn't handle the event in question, we'll process it # as an unimplemented event if not event_was_handled : self . process_unimplemented_event ( event ) every_event_was_handled = False return dispatched_event_count > 0 and every_event_was_handled

Args: command_line_target_fps: The --target-fps value, or None if it was not passed. game: The game scene class or instance, which may declare TARGET_FPS. Returns: float: The effective target FPS (0 means uncapped). Raises: TypeError: If the game's TARGET_FPS is neither None nor a (non-bool) number. ValueError: If the game's TARGET_FPS is negative, NaN or infinite. """ if command_line_target_fps is not None : return float ( command_line_target_fps ) game_target_fps = getattr ( game , 'TARGET_FPS' , None ) if game_target_fps is None : return DEFAULT_TARGET_FPS scene_class = game if isinstance ( game , type ) else type ( game ) # bool is a subclass of int, so it must be rejected explicitly. if isinstance ( game_target_fps , bool ) or not isinstance ( game_target_fps , ( int , float )): message = ( f ' { scene_class . __name__ } .TARGET_FPS must be a number or None, ' f 'got { game_target_fps !r} ' ) raise TypeError ( message ) if not math . isfinite ( game_target_fps ) or game_target_fps < 0 : message = ( f ' { scene_class . __name__ } .TARGET_FPS must be a finite number >= 0 ' f '(0 = uncapped), got { game_target_fps !r} ' ) raise ValueError ( message ) return float ( game_target_fps )

docs.text: Start the game engine. However the run ends, the teardown ( _shutdown : recordings closed) runs first; if the teardown itself raises, the run exits ExitCode.INTERNAL_ERROR (both errors logged). An exception raised before start(), in __init__ , is not mapped: it exits with Python's default 1 (each game has its own entry point, so there is no one place to wrap; see glitchygames/exit_codes.py). A replay ( --replay-trace ) that ends normally exits with its own code ( ReplayResult.exit_code under its exit policy), watched or headless. Raises: RuntimeError – If the game is not initialized. SystemExit – With ExitCode.INTERNAL_ERROR after an uncaught exception (logged with its traceback), ExitCode.INTERRUPTED after Ctrl-C (KeyboardInterrupt), or whatever status a SystemExit raised during the run carries (a signal handler's, a game's own), except a game's own successful exit that cuts a replay short ( ExitCode.REPLAY_DIVERGED ; a rebaseline ends normally then, with what the game ran); at the normal end of a replay, with the replay's exit code ( ExitCode.SUCCESS , ExitCode.REPLAY_DIVERGED or ExitCode.UNUSABLE_INPUT for a truncated recording). Source code in glitchygames/engine/game_engine.py 2184 2185 2186 2187 2188 2189 2190 2191 2192 2193 2194 2195 2196 2197 2198 2199 2200 2201 2202 2203 2204 2205 2206 2207 2208 2209 2210 2211 2212 2213 2214 2215 2216 2217 2218 2219 2220 2221 2222 2223 2224 2225 2226 2227 2228 2229 2230 2231 2232 2233 2234 2235 2236 2237 2238 2239 2240 2241 2242 2243 2244 2245 2246 2247 2248 2249 2250 2251 2252 2253 def start ( self : Self ) -> None : """Start the game engine. However the run ends, the teardown (``_shutdown``: recordings closed) runs first; if the teardown itself raises, the run exits ``ExitCode.INTERNAL_ERROR`` (both errors logged). An exception raised before start(), in ``__init__``, is not mapped: it exits with Python's default 1 (each game has its own entry point, so there is no one place to wrap; see glitchygames/exit_codes.py). A replay (``--replay-trace``) that ends normally exits with its own code (``ReplayResult.exit_code`` under its exit policy), watched or headless. Raises: RuntimeError: If the game is not initialized. SystemExit: With ``ExitCode.INTERNAL_ERROR`` after an uncaught exception (logged with its traceback), ``ExitCode.INTERRUPTED`` after Ctrl-C (KeyboardInterrupt), or whatever status a SystemExit raised during the run carries (a signal handler's, a game's own), except a game's own successful exit that cuts a replay short (``ExitCode.REPLAY_DIVERGED``; a rebaseline ends normally then, with what the game ran); at the normal end of a replay, with the replay's exit code (``ExitCode.SUCCESS``, ``ExitCode.REPLAY_DIVERGED`` or ``ExitCode.UNUSABLE_INPUT`` for a truncated recording). """ # This ensures that logging is enabled as soon as the game object is created. logging . getLogger ( 'game' ) self . log . info ( f 'Starting game engine for game: { type ( self ) . NAME } ' ) if self . game is None : raise RuntimeError ( GAME_NOT_INITIALIZED_MSG ) profiler = None if GameEngine . OPTIONS [ 'profile' ]: # Enabled before the crash boundary, so the teardown prints only a profiler that ran profiler = cProfile . Profile () profiler . enable () # Set when the run ends in a way that start() turns into an exit code exit_code : ExitCode | None = None run_error : Exception | None = None # What ended the run early, described for the replay report (None: a normal end) run_ended_by : str | None = None try : # The crash boundary: anything the run raises is turned into an exit code below self . _run_game () except KeyboardInterrupt : # Ctrl-C: never an internal error; exits INTERRUPTED once the teardown has run exit_code = ExitCode . INTERRUPTED run_ended_by = exit_code . describe () except SystemExit as exit_request : # A deliberate exit (a signal handler's, a game's) keeps its status run_ended_by = self . _describe_exit_request ( exit_status = exit_request . code ) if not self . _exit_cuts_a_replay_short ( exit_status = exit_request . code ): raise exit_code , run_ended_by = self . _outcome_of_a_replay_cut_short ( run_ended_by = run_ended_by ) except RecordingWriteError as error : # The disk filled part way: logged on one line by the recorder (BUGS.md #82) exit_code = ExitCode . CANNOT_WRITE_OUTPUT run_ended_by = exit_code . describe () run_error = error except Exception as error : scene_name = self . _resolve_scene_name_for_error () self . log . exception ( "Runtime error during game execution @ scene ' %s '" , scene_name ) exit_code = ExitCode . INTERNAL_ERROR run_ended_by = exit_code . describe () run_error = error finally : teardown_error = self . _tear_down_run ( profiler = profiler , run_ended_by = run_ended_by ) if teardown_error is not None : # Replaces whatever was ending the run: a failed teardown is an internal error exit_with ( exit_code = ExitCode . INTERNAL_ERROR , cause = teardown_error ) self . _end_run ( exit_code = exit_code , run_error = run_error )

docs.text: Start recording the session to a trace file (before the first frame). The header also holds what the run took in before recording started: a snapshot of every save store the doors opened ( saves ), the descriptors of devices opened ( devices ) and the enumeration answers given ( device_enumeration ). Then RecordingSources are installed around the active doors and record every frame from what passes through them (glitchygames/recording.py). SIGTERM (and SIGHUP on Unix, SIGBREAK on Windows) ends a started run through the normal teardown ( exit_on_signal , installed by start ), and so does SIGINT (KeyboardInterrupt). stop_trace_recording (called by _shutdown ) closes the file. Recording must start before the first frame: afterwards installing its doors raises SourcesAlreadyRunningError (from install_sources ; glitchygames/sources.py). Parameters: path ( Path ) – The recording's file. Returns: GameplayRecorder – The recorder. Raises: TraceRecordingAlreadyStartedError – If this engine is already recording. Source code in glitchygames/engine/game_engine.py 1558 1559 1560 1561 1562 1563 1564 1565 1566 1567 1568 1569 1570 1571 1572 1573 1574 1575 1576 1577 1578 1579 1580 1581 1582 1583 1584 1585 1586 1587 1588 1589 1590 1591 1592 1593 1594 1595 1596 1597 1598 1599 1600 1601 1602 1603 1604 1605 1606 1607 1608 1609 1610 1611 1612 1613 1614 1615 1616 1617 1618 1619 def start_trace_recording ( self : Self , * , path : Path ) -> GameplayRecorder : """Start recording the session to a trace file (before the first frame). The header also holds what the run took in before recording started: a snapshot of every save store the doors opened (``saves``), the descriptors of devices opened (``devices``) and the enumeration answers given (``device_enumeration``). Then ``RecordingSources`` are installed around the active doors and record every frame from what passes through them (glitchygames/recording.py). SIGTERM (and SIGHUP on Unix, SIGBREAK on Windows) ends a started run through the normal teardown (``exit_on_signal``, installed by ``start``), and so does SIGINT (KeyboardInterrupt). ``stop_trace_recording`` (called by ``_shutdown``) closes the file. Recording must start before the first frame: afterwards installing its doors raises ``SourcesAlreadyRunningError`` (from ``install_sources``; glitchygames/sources.py). Args: path: The recording's file. Returns: The recorder. Raises: TraceRecordingAlreadyStartedError: If this engine is already recording. """ if self . trace_recorder is not None : message = ( f 'start_trace_recording() was called while recording to ' f ' { self . trace_recorder . path } ; one run records once' ) raise TraceRecordingAlreadyStartedError ( message ) inner = active_sources () registry = inner . devices () # A store a run started with --record-trace opened before recording started is in the # header as first opened: the first scene's setup() may have written to it since, and # the replay runs that setup() again (LiveSources.first_open_save_snapshots) first_open_snapshots : Mapping [ str , dict [ str , Any ]] = ( inner . first_open_save_snapshots if isinstance ( inner , LiveSources ) else {} ) # A rebaseline copies these fields from the replayed recording instead (rebaseline.py) header = { ** self . trace_recording_header (), SAVES_HEADER_FIELD : { namespace : ( first_open_snapshots [ namespace ] if namespace in first_open_snapshots else save_namespace_snapshot ( saves = store ) ) for namespace , store in inner . opened_save_namespaces . items () }, DEVICES_HEADER_FIELD : [ descriptor . to_json () for descriptor in registry . take_opened_descriptors () ], DEVICE_ENUMERATION_FIELD : [ answer . to_json () for answer in registry . take_enumeration_answers () ], } recorder = GameplayRecorder ( path = path , header = header ) install_sources ( sources = RecordingSources ( inner = inner , recorder = recorder )) self . trace_recorder = recorder self . log . info ( f 'Recording gameplay to { path } (random seed { self . random_seed } )' ) return recorder

docs.text: Override the default subclasshook to create an interface. A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass even without inheriting from it. Per the abc contract, anything else returns NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods, so the structural check never passes for it). Returns: bool ( bool ) – True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented (typeshed annotates object. subclasshook as bool and types NotImplemented as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides. Source code in glitchygames/events/base.py 555 556 557 558 559 560 561 562 563 564 565 566 567 568 569 570 571 572 573 574 575 576 577 578 579 580 581 582 583 584 585 586 587 588 589 590 591 592 593 594 595 596 597 598 599 @classmethod @override def __subclasshook__ ( cls , subclass : type [ Any ]) -> bool : """Override the default __subclasshook__ to create an interface. A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass even without inheriting from it. Per the `abc` contract, anything else returns NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods, so the structural check never passes for it). Returns: bool: True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented (typeshed annotates object.__subclasshook__ as bool and types NotImplemented as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides. """ # Note: This accounts for under/dunder methods in addition to regular methods. interface_attributes = set ( cls . __abstractmethods__ ) abstract_methods = getattr ( subclass , '__abstractmethods__' , frozenset [ str ]()) subclass_attributes : set [ str ] = set ( abstract_methods ) interface_is_implemented = False methods : list [ bool ] = [] for attribute in sorted ( interface_attributes ): if hasattr ( subclass , attribute ) and attribute not in subclass_attributes : if callable ( getattr ( subclass , attribute )): cls . log . debug ( f ' { subclass . __name__ } . { attribute } -> implemented (callable)' ) else : cls . log . debug ( f ' { subclass . __name__ } . { attribute } -> implemented (attribute)' ) methods . append ( True ) else : cls . log . debug ( f ' { subclass . __name__ } . { attribute } -> unimplemented' ) methods . append ( False ) # all([]) returns True, so mask it # # This protects against an empty attribute list # which would be a misconfiguration of the interface if len ( methods ) > 0 and all ( methods ): interface_is_implemented = all ( methods ) if interface_is_implemented : return True return NotImplemented

docs.text: End the run with SystemExit, so GameEngine.start()'s teardown still runs. Installed by GameEngine.start for each of terminating_signals() that nothing else handles, for the whole run, so a recording is closed by _shutdown . It ignores further signals of the same kind before raising: a second SIGTERM ( uv run forwards one to its child as well, and pkill can match both) would otherwise raise again inside the teardown and leave the recording unclosed. _shutdown restores the default handling after closing the recording. It does nothing else: logging here could fail with "reentrant call" if the signal interrupted a write to the same stream. Parameters: signal_number ( int ) – The signal received. _frame ( FrameType | None ) – The interrupted frame (unused). Raises: SystemExit – Always, with ExitCode.for_signal(signal_number) ( TERMINATED for SIGTERM, HANGUP for SIGHUP, BREAK for SIGBREAK). Source code in glitchygames/engine/game_engine.py 266 267 268 269 270 271 272 273 274 275 276 277 278 279 280 281 282 283 284 285 286 287 def exit_on_signal ( signal_number : int , _frame : FrameType | None ) -> None : """End the run with SystemExit, so GameEngine.start()'s teardown still runs. Installed by ``GameEngine.start`` for each of ``terminating_signals()`` that nothing else handles, for the whole run, so a recording is closed by ``_shutdown``. It ignores further signals of the same kind before raising: a second SIGTERM (``uv run`` forwards one to its child as well, and ``pkill`` can match both) would otherwise raise again inside the teardown and leave the recording unclosed. ``_shutdown`` restores the default handling after closing the recording. It does nothing else: logging here could fail with "reentrant call" if the signal interrupted a write to the same stream. Args: signal_number: The signal received. _frame: The interrupted frame (unused). Raises: SystemExit: Always, with ``ExitCode.for_signal(signal_number)`` (``TERMINATED`` for SIGTERM, ``HANGUP`` for SIGHUP, ``BREAK`` for SIGBREAK). """ signal . signal ( signal_number , signal . SIG_IGN ) raise SystemExit ( ExitCode . for_signal ( signal_number ))

docs.text: Return each event's origin in the doors' last batch, when a replay's merge knows them. A recorder over a replay ( --rebaseline ) takes them from the replay, and so does the instant-replay journal (glitchygames/instant_replay.py, rule 4): a watched replay's held frames drain the real queue between pumps, so the posts pending before a pump do not tell them. Parameters: doors ( EngineSources ) – The doors that pumped (the run's installed ones, or a recording around them). Returns: list [ str ] | None – The origins, or None when the doors are not a replay's. Source code in glitchygames/engine/game_engine.py 305 306 307 308 309 310 311 312 313 314 315 316 317 318 319 320 321 322 323 324 def replayed_batch_origins ( * , doors : EngineSources ) -> list [ str ] | None : """Return each event's origin in the doors' last batch, when a replay's merge knows them. A recorder over a replay (``--rebaseline``) takes them from the replay, and so does the instant-replay journal (glitchygames/instant_replay.py, rule 4): a watched replay's held frames drain the real queue between pumps, so the posts pending before a pump do not tell them. Args: doors: The doors that pumped (the run's installed ones, or a recording around them). Returns: The origins, or None when the doors are not a replay's. """ while isinstance ( doors , RecordingSources ): doors = doors . inner if isinstance ( doors , ReplaySources ): return doors . last_batch_origins () return None

IntEnum ): """The process exit codes of the engine, the replay tools and the API client.""" # Success; the replay matched; the audit is deterministic. Same value as Python's os.EX_OK # (sysexits.h EX_OK) SUCCESS = 0 # A replay's frames differ from the recording REPLAY_DIVERGED = 1 # argparse's own status for a usage error. The engine never exits with it: it is named for # callers and tests that tell argparse's refusals from the engine's ARGUMENT_PARSER_ERROR = 2 # --audit's two replay runs differ from each other or from the recording AUDIT_NONDETERMINISTIC = 3 # The API server rejected the client's sprite generation (an error status, or a response that # says it failed) GENERATION_REJECTED = 4 # The API server rejected the client's frame extraction (an error status, or a response that # says it failed) EXTRACTION_REJECTED = 5 # scripts/audio_glitch_probe.py found a risk of audio dropouts AUDIO_DROPOUT_RISK = 6 # --rebaseline wrote the new recording, but the run never received some of the old one's # input (glitchygames/replay/rebaseline.py, rule 2) REBASELINE_INPUT_LOST = 7 # A replay matched, but took longer to process than --max-processing-slowdown allows; see # glitchygames/replay/processing.py PROCESSING_SLOWER = 8 # The engine refuses the options given (a combination it will not run). Same value as # Python's os.EX_USAGE (sysexits.h EX_USAGE) OPTIONS_REFUSED = 64 # The recording or input data is unusable. Same value as Python's os.EX_DATAERR (sysexits.h # EX_DATAERR) UNUSABLE_INPUT = 65 # The input file does not exist. Same value as Python's os.EX_NOINPUT (sysexits.h EX_NOINPUT) MISSING_INPUT = 66 # A required service (the API server) cannot be reached. Same value as Python's # os.EX_UNAVAILABLE (sysexits.h EX_UNAVAILABLE) SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE = 69 # An uncaught exception during a run, or an audit that could not run. Same value as Python's # os.EX_SOFTWARE (sysexits.h EX_SOFTWARE) INTERNAL_ERROR = 70 # An output file or directory cannot be created or written. Same value as Python's # os.EX_CANTCREAT (sysexits.h EX_CANTCREAT) CANNOT_WRITE_OUTPUT = 73 # Stopped by SIGHUP (Unix only): 128 + signal.SIGHUP HANGUP = 129 # Stopped by SIGINT (Ctrl-C): 128 + signal.SIGINT INTERRUPTED = 130 # Stopped by SIGTERM: 128 + signal.SIGTERM TERMINATED = 143 # Stopped by SIGBREAK (Windows only: Ctrl-Break): 128 + signal.SIGBREAK BREAK = 149 @classmethod def for_signal ( cls , signal_number : int ) -> ExitCode : """Return the member a run stopped by a signal exits with. Args: signal_number: The signal (``signal.SIGTERM`` and so on). Returns: ``HANGUP``, ``INTERRUPTED``, ``TERMINATED`` or ``BREAK``. Raises: ValueError: For a signal the engine does not wire (see the module docstring), rather than a number with no name. """ message = f 'signal { signal_number } has no exit code: the engine does not handle it' if signal_number <= 0 : raise ValueError ( message ) try : return cls ( SIGNAL_EXIT_STATUS_BASE + signal_number ) except ValueError as error : raise ValueError ( message ) from error def describe ( self ) -> str : """Return the code's name and number, as logs show it. ``str()`` of an IntEnum member is only its number (Python 3.11 on). Returns: For example ``'OPTIONS_REFUSED (64)'``. """ return f ' { self . name } ( { self . value } )' @classmethod def describe_status ( cls , status : int ) -> str : """Describe any process exit status: a member, a signal exit, or an unknown number. Args: status: A process's exit status (a child's ``returncode``). Returns: ``'INTERNAL_ERROR (70)'`` for a member; for a signal, ``'signal 6 (134)'`` (128 + the signal number, as a shell reports it) or, for a process killed by the signal (a subprocess reports -N), ``'TERMINATED (signal 15)'`` where the signal has a member and ``'signal 6'`` otherwise; any other number alone. """ if status < 0 : signal_number = - status try : return f ' { cls . for_signal ( signal_number ) . name } (signal { signal_number } )' except ValueError : return f 'signal { signal_number } ' try : return cls ( status ) . describe () except ValueError : pass if status > SIGNAL_EXIT_STATUS_BASE : return f 'signal { status - SIGNAL_EXIT_STATUS_BASE } ( { status } )' return str ( status )

QUIT : self . log . info ( 'Window close requested' ) self . scene_manager . quit_requested = True return # Check if there are any focused sprites in the current scene scene = self . scene_manager . active_scene if scene and scene . all_sprites : focused_sprites = [ sprite for sprite in scene . all_sprites if hasattr ( sprite , 'is_active' ) and sprite . is_active ] # If we have focused sprites, ALL key events go to the scene if focused_sprites and event . type == pygame . KEYDOWN : self . scene_manager . handle_event ( event ) return # Only handle engine-level key events if no focused sprites if event . type == pygame . KEYDOWN and getattr ( event , 'key' , None ) == pygame . K_q : self . log . info ( 'Quit key pressed with no focused sprites' ) self . scene_manager . quit_requested = True return # Pass other events to the scene manager self . scene_manager . handle_event ( event )

Each event is judged on its own; an event whose type has no entry in EVENT_HANDLERS , or whose handler did not handle it, goes to process_unimplemented_event . Parameters: should_discard ( Callable [[ Event ], bool ] | None , default: None ) – Returns True for an event to remove from the batch without processing it (not counted as unhandled). SceneManager passes is_discarded_during_transition during a transition. Returns: bool ( bool ) – True if at least one event was dispatched and every dispatched event was bool – handled (a raw-event scene's process_event counts as handled). Event ], bool ] | None = None ) -> bool : """Process every event queued this frame. ``pygame.event.get()`` removes the whole batch from SDL's queue at once, so every event of the batch is handled here: none may be dropped. Each event is judged on its own; an event whose type has no entry in ``EVENT_HANDLERS``, or whose handler did not handle it, goes to ``process_unimplemented_event``. Args: should_discard: Returns True for an event to remove from the batch without processing it (not counted as unhandled). SceneManager passes ``is_discarded_during_transition`` during a transition. Returns: bool: True if at least one event was dispatched and every dispatched event was handled (a raw-event scene's ``process_event`` counts as handled). False if any dispatched event was unhandled, or if nothing was dispatched: an empty batch, or one whose events were all discarded. """ raw_events = self . _pump_events () # Polled input is read once per frame, right after the pump, so it agrees with this # frame's events; it stays fixed until the next frame's pump, so dt_tick (which runs # before this) reads the previous frame's snapshot (glitchygames/input/state.py) set_current_input ( snapshot = active_sources () . input_snapshot ()) dispatched_event_count = 0 every_event_was_handled = True for pygame_event in raw_events : if should_discard is not None and should_discard ( pygame_event ): continue dispatched_event_count += 1 # Support scenes processing pygame raw events, bypassing # the glitchygames.engine event processing altogether if hasattr ( self . _active_scene , 'process_event' ): self . _active_scene . process_event ( pygame_event ) # type: ignore[union-attr] # ty: ignore[call-non-callable] continue event : events . HashableEvent = events . HashableEvent ( type = pygame_event . type ) event . __dict__ . update ( pygame_event . dict ) # Decided per event: a type missing from the map is unhandled event_was_handled = False if event . type in GameEngine . EVENT_HANDLERS : event_was_handled = bool ( GameEngine . EVENT_HANDLERS [ event . type ]( event )) # If an event is not in the event handler map, or the function # called didn't handle the event in question, we'll process it # as an unimplemented event if not event_was_handled : self . process_unimplemented_event ( event ) every_event_was_handled = False return dispatched_event_count > 0 and every_event_was_handled

""" if command_line_target_fps is not None : return float ( command_line_target_fps ) game_target_fps = getattr ( game , 'TARGET_FPS' , None ) if game_target_fps is None : return DEFAULT_TARGET_FPS scene_class = game if isinstance ( game , type ) else type ( game ) # bool is a subclass of int, so it must be rejected explicitly. if isinstance ( game_target_fps , bool ) or not isinstance ( game_target_fps , ( int , float )): message = ( f ' { scene_class . __name__ } .TARGET_FPS must be a number or None, ' f 'got { game_target_fps !r} ' ) raise TypeError ( message ) if not math . isfinite ( game_target_fps ) or game_target_fps < 0 : message = ( f ' { scene_class . __name__ } .TARGET_FPS must be a finite number >= 0 ' f '(0 = uncapped), got { game_target_fps !r} ' ) raise ValueError ( message ) return float ( game_target_fps )

docs.text: Start the game engine. However the run ends, the teardown ( _shutdown : recordings closed) runs first; if the teardown itself raises, the run exits ExitCode.INTERNAL_ERROR (both errors logged). An exception raised before start(), in __init__ , is not mapped: it exits with Python's default 1 (each game has its own entry point, so there is no one place to wrap; see glitchygames/exit_codes.py). A replay ( --replay-trace ) that ends normally exits with its own code ( ReplayResult.exit_code under its exit policy), watched or headless. Raises: RuntimeError – If the game is not initialized. SystemExit – With ExitCode.INTERNAL_ERROR after an uncaught exception (logged with its traceback), ExitCode.INTERRUPTED after Ctrl-C (KeyboardInterrupt), or whatever status a SystemExit raised during the run carries (a signal handler's, a game's own), except a game's own successful exit that cuts a replay short ( ExitCode.REPLAY_DIVERGED ; a rebaseline ends normally then, with what the game ran); at the normal end of a replay, with the replay's exit code ( ExitCode.SUCCESS , ExitCode.REPLAY_DIVERGED or ExitCode.UNUSABLE_INPUT for a truncated recording). Source code in glitchygames/engine/game_engine.py 2184 2185 2186 2187 2188 2189 2190 2191 2192 2193 2194 2195 2196 2197 2198 2199 2200 2201 2202 2203 2204 2205 2206 2207 2208 2209 2210 2211 2212 2213 2214 2215 2216 2217 2218 2219 2220 2221 2222 2223 2224 2225 2226 2227 2228 2229 2230 2231 2232 2233 2234 2235 2236 2237 2238 2239 2240 2241 2242 2243 2244 2245 2246 2247 2248 2249 2250 2251 2252 2253 def start ( self : Self ) -> None : """Start the game engine. However the run ends, the teardown (``_shutdown``: recordings closed) runs first; if the teardown itself raises, the run exits ``ExitCode.INTERNAL_ERROR`` (both errors logged). An exception raised before start(), in ``__init__``, is not mapped: it exits with Python's default 1 (each game has its own entry point, so there is no one place to wrap; see glitchygames/exit_codes.py). A replay (``--replay-trace``) that ends normally exits with its own code (``ReplayResult.exit_code`` under its exit policy), watched or headless. Raises: RuntimeError: If the game is not initialized. SystemExit: With ``ExitCode.INTERNAL_ERROR`` after an uncaught exception (logged with its traceback), ``ExitCode.INTERRUPTED`` after Ctrl-C (KeyboardInterrupt), or whatever status a SystemExit raised during the run carries (a signal handler's, a game's own), except a game's own successful exit that cuts a replay short (``ExitCode.REPLAY_DIVERGED``; a rebaseline ends normally then, with what the game ran); at the normal end of a replay, with the replay's exit code (``ExitCode.SUCCESS``, ``ExitCode.REPLAY_DIVERGED`` or ``ExitCode.UNUSABLE_INPUT`` for a truncated recording). """ # This ensures that logging is enabled as soon as the game object is created. logging . getLogger ( 'game' ) self . log . info ( f 'Starting game engine for game: { type ( self ) . NAME } ' ) if self . game is None : raise RuntimeError ( GAME_NOT_INITIALIZED_MSG ) profiler = None if GameEngine . OPTIONS [ 'profile' ]: # Enabled before the crash boundary, so the teardown prints only a profiler that ran profiler = cProfile . Profile () profiler . enable () # Set when the run ends in a way that start() turns into an exit code exit_code : ExitCode | None = None run_error : Exception | None = None # What ended the run early, described for the replay report (None: a normal end) run_ended_by : str | None = None try : # The crash boundary: anything the run raises is turned into an exit code below self . _run_game () except KeyboardInterrupt : # Ctrl-C: never an internal error; exits INTERRUPTED once the teardown has run exit_code = ExitCode . INTERRUPTED run_ended_by = exit_code . describe () except SystemExit as exit_request : # A deliberate exit (a signal handler's, a game's) keeps its status run_ended_by = self . _describe_exit_request ( exit_status = exit_request . code ) if not self . _exit_cuts_a_replay_short ( exit_status = exit_request . code ): raise exit_code , run_ended_by = self . _outcome_of_a_replay_cut_short ( run_ended_by = run_ended_by ) except RecordingWriteError as error : # The disk filled part way: logged on one line by the recorder (BUGS.md #82) exit_code = ExitCode . CANNOT_WRITE_OUTPUT run_ended_by = exit_code . describe () run_error = error except Exception as error : scene_name = self . _resolve_scene_name_for_error () self . log . exception ( "Runtime error during game execution @ scene ' %s '" , scene_name ) exit_code = ExitCode . INTERNAL_ERROR run_ended_by = exit_code . describe () run_error = error finally : teardown_error = self . _tear_down_run ( profiler = profiler , run_ended_by = run_ended_by ) if teardown_error is not None : # Replaces whatever was ending the run: a failed teardown is an internal error exit_with ( exit_code = ExitCode . INTERNAL_ERROR , cause = teardown_error ) self . _end_run ( exit_code = exit_code , run_error = run_error )

docs.text: Start recording the session to a trace file (before the first frame). The header also holds what the run took in before recording started: a snapshot of every save store the doors opened ( saves ), the descriptors of devices opened ( devices ) and the enumeration answers given ( device_enumeration ). Then RecordingSources are installed around the active doors and record every frame from what passes through them (glitchygames/recording.py). SIGTERM (and SIGHUP on Unix, SIGBREAK on Windows) ends a started run through the normal teardown ( exit_on_signal , installed by start ), and so does SIGINT (KeyboardInterrupt). stop_trace_recording (called by _shutdown ) closes the file. Recording must start before the first frame: afterwards installing its doors raises SourcesAlreadyRunningError (from install_sources ; glitchygames/sources.py). Parameters: path ( Path ) – The recording's file. Returns: GameplayRecorder – The recorder. Raises: TraceRecordingAlreadyStartedError – If this engine is already recording. Source code in glitchygames/engine/game_engine.py 1558 1559 1560 1561 1562 1563 1564 1565 1566 1567 1568 1569 1570 1571 1572 1573 1574 1575 1576 1577 1578 1579 1580 1581 1582 1583 1584 1585 1586 1587 1588 1589 1590 1591 1592 1593 1594 1595 1596 1597 1598 1599 1600 1601 1602 1603 1604 1605 1606 1607 1608 1609 1610 1611 1612 1613 1614 1615 1616 1617 1618 1619 def start_trace_recording ( self : Self , * , path : Path ) -> GameplayRecorder : """Start recording the session to a trace file (before the first frame). The header also holds what the run took in before recording started: a snapshot of every save store the doors opened (``saves``), the descriptors of devices opened (``devices``) and the enumeration answers given (``device_enumeration``). Then ``RecordingSources`` are installed around the active doors and record every frame from what passes through them (glitchygames/recording.py). SIGTERM (and SIGHUP on Unix, SIGBREAK on Windows) ends a started run through the normal teardown (``exit_on_signal``, installed by ``start``), and so does SIGINT (KeyboardInterrupt). ``stop_trace_recording`` (called by ``_shutdown``) closes the file. Recording must start before the first frame: afterwards installing its doors raises ``SourcesAlreadyRunningError`` (from ``install_sources``; glitchygames/sources.py). Args: path: The recording's file. Returns: The recorder. Raises: TraceRecordingAlreadyStartedError: If this engine is already recording. """ if self . trace_recorder is not None : message = ( f 'start_trace_recording() was called while recording to ' f ' { self . trace_recorder . path } ; one run records once' ) raise TraceRecordingAlreadyStartedError ( message ) inner = active_sources () registry = inner . devices () # A store a run started with --record-trace opened before recording started is in the # header as first opened: the first scene's setup() may have written to it since, and # the replay runs that setup() again (LiveSources.first_open_save_snapshots) first_open_snapshots : Mapping [ str , dict [ str , Any ]] = ( inner . first_open_save_snapshots if isinstance ( inner , LiveSources ) else {} ) # A rebaseline copies these fields from the replayed recording instead (rebaseline.py) header = { ** self . trace_recording_header (), SAVES_HEADER_FIELD : { namespace : ( first_open_snapshots [ namespace ] if namespace in first_open_snapshots else save_namespace_snapshot ( saves = store ) ) for namespace , store in inner . opened_save_namespaces . items () }, DEVICES_HEADER_FIELD : [ descriptor . to_json () for descriptor in registry . take_opened_descriptors () ], DEVICE_ENUMERATION_FIELD : [ answer . to_json () for answer in registry . take_enumeration_answers () ], } recorder = GameplayRecorder ( path = path , header = header ) install_sources ( sources = RecordingSources ( inner = inner , recorder = recorder )) self . trace_recorder = recorder self . log . info ( f 'Recording gameplay to { path } (random seed { self . random_seed } )' ) return recorder

docs.text: Describe every unhandled event type, most frequent first. Each line names the type (pygame's event name and its number, so custom and unknown types still show), its count, when it was first seen and the first event's attribute names, e.g. JOYDEVICEADDED (1541) x1, first at 0.3 s, attributes: device_index, guid . Returns: list [ str ] – One line per type; empty when every event was handled. Source code in glitchygames/engine/game_engine.py 3129 3130 3131 3132 3133 3134 3135 3136 3137 3138 3139 3140 3141 3142 3143 3144 3145 3146 3147 3148 3149 3150 def unhandled_event_report ( self : Self ) -> list [ str ]: """Describe every unhandled event type, most frequent first. Each line names the type (pygame's event name and its number, so custom and unknown types still show), its count, when it was first seen and the first event's attribute names, e.g. ``JOYDEVICEADDED (1541) x1, first at 0.3 s, attributes: device_index, guid``. Returns: One line per type; empty when every event was handled. """ records = sorted ( self . unhandled_events . items (), key = lambda item : item [ 1 ] . count , reverse = True , ) return [ f ' { pygame . event . event_name ( event_type ) . upper () } ( { event_type } ) x { record . count } , ' f 'first at { record . first_seen_seconds : .1f } s, ' f 'attributes: { ", " . join ( record . attribute_names ) or "none" } ' for event_type , record in records ]

docs.text: Override the default subclasshook to create an interface. A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass even without inheriting from it. Per the abc contract, anything else returns NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods, so the structural check never passes for it). Returns: bool ( bool ) – True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented (typeshed annotates object. subclasshook as bool and types NotImplemented as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides. Source code in glitchygames/events/base.py 555 556 557 558 559 560 561 562 563 564 565 566 567 568 569 570 571 572 573 574 575 576 577 578 579 580 581 582 583 584 585 586 587 588 589 590 591 592 593 594 595 596 597 598 599 @classmethod @override def __subclasshook__ ( cls , subclass : type [ Any ]) -> bool : """Override the default __subclasshook__ to create an interface. A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass even without inheriting from it. Per the `abc` contract, anything else returns NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods, so the structural check never passes for it). Returns: bool: True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented (typeshed annotates object.__subclasshook__ as bool and types NotImplemented as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides. """ # Note: This accounts for under/dunder methods in addition to regular methods. interface_attributes = set ( cls . __abstractmethods__ ) abstract_methods = getattr ( subclass , '__abstractmethods__' , frozenset [ str ]()) subclass_attributes : set [ str ] = set ( abstract_methods ) interface_is_implemented = False methods : list [ bool ] = [] for attribute in sorted ( interface_attributes ): if hasattr ( subclass , attribute ) and attribute not in subclass_attributes : if callable ( getattr ( subclass , attribute )): cls . log . debug ( f ' { subclass . __name__ } . { attribute } -> implemented (callable)' ) else : cls . log . debug ( f ' { subclass . __name__ } . { attribute } -> implemented (attribute)' ) methods . append ( True ) else : cls . log . debug ( f ' { subclass . __name__ } . { attribute } -> unimplemented' ) methods . append ( False ) # all([]) returns True, so mask it # # This protects against an empty attribute list # which would be a misconfiguration of the interface if len ( methods ) > 0 and all ( methods ): interface_is_implemented = all ( methods ) if interface_is_implemented : return True return NotImplemented
